Spencer committed to [[Purdue University]] on July 8, 2003.<ref>{{cite web |title=Anthony Spencer |url=https://n.rivals.com/content/prospects/maple/1300 |publisher=Rivals.com |access-date=November 15, 2016}}</ref> He also had [[Football Bowl Subdivision|FBS]] scholarship offers from [[Michigan State Spartans football|Michigan State]].

==College career==
Spencer accepted a scholarship to play [[college football]] at [[Purdue University]]. He spent the 2002 season on the Purdue [[scout team]] as a [[redshirt freshman]]. He appeared in ten games during the 2003 season, recording six tackles and one stop behind the [[line of scrimmage]].

In 2004, Spencer played in 12 games and [[Starting lineup|started]] in 11. He registered 33 tackles and finished third on the team with 7.5 sacks and 9.5 stops for losses. He also batted down six passes and forced three fumbles, earning [[List of All-Big Ten Conference football teams|All-Big Ten Conference]] honorable mention.

Even though he started all 11 games in 2005, Spencer failed to match his 2004 performance due to several minor injuries. He was limited to 23 tackles, three sacks, and 7.5 stops behind the line of scrimmage. He caused three fumbles and recovered another while also deflecting one pass.

Spencer had a great senior season in 2006. He finished the season ranked second in the nation with 26.5 stops behind the line of scrimmage, the fifth-best season total in Big Ten Conference history.  He finished second on the team with 93 tackles (a high number for a defensive lineman) and first with 10.5 sacks. He also caused five fumbles and recovered another while batting away six passes and blocking one kick. He was named the Purdue football team's [[Most Valuable Player]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://news-sentinel.com/sports/Fort-Wayne-s-All-Time-Greatest-Series--Anthony-Spencer--DL |title=Fort Wayne's All-Time Greatest Series: Anthony Spencer, DL |publisher=News-Sentinel.com |date=September 18, 2016 |access-date=December 20, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170318173235/http://news-sentinel.com/sports/Fort-Wayne-s-All-Time-Greatest-Series--Anthony-Spencer--DL |archive-date=March 18, 2017 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

As a former Indiana high school all-star who also excelled at Purdue, Spencer was co-recipient of the 2007 Rabold Award given by the Indiana Football Coaches Association.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://ifca.zebras.net/ifca/candler/announcements/service_awards.htm |title=Indiana Football Coaches Association Service Awards |publisher=Ifca.zebras.net |access-date=December 20, 2016 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304041845/http://ifca.zebras.net/ifca/candler/announcements/service_awards.htm |archive-date=March 4, 2016 }}</ref> Spencer also was invited to play in the [[2007 Senior Bowl]].

Spencer received a degree in [[African-American Studies]], with a minor in Law & Society.

==Professional career==
===Dallas Cowboys===

====2007 season====
Spencer was [[NFL draft|selected]] in the first round with the 26th overall pick by the [[Dallas Cowboys]] in the [[2007 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=2007 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2007/draft.htm |access-date=2023-05-10 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> After trading their first round selection to the [[Cleveland Browns]], the Cowboys traded back into the first round to draft him. The Cowboys traded their 2007 second-round pick (#36-[[Kevin Kolb]]), 2007 third-round pick (#87-[[Stewart Bradley (American football)|Stewart Bradley]]) and a 2007 fifth-round pick (#159-[[C.J. Gaddis]]) to their division rival [[Philadelphia Eagles]], in exchange for their 1st-round pick (26th overall).<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.dallascowboys.com/news/2007/04/28/spencer-gives-cowboys-yet-another-pass-rusher |title=Spencer Gives Cowboys Yet Another Pass Rusher | publisher=DallasCowboys.com - John Newbern | access-date=May 1, 2016}}</ref>

Spencer was converted to an [[outside linebacker]] and named the starter opposite to [[DeMarcus Ware]], while [[Greg Ellis (American football)|Greg Ellis]] was recovering from his Achilles surgery. He started the first six games of the season, becoming only the fourth rookie linebacker in franchise history to start in a season-opener ([[Lee Roy Jordan]], [[Robert Jones (linebacker)|Robert Jones]], Ware).

He played in all 16 regular season games and Cowboys' playoff game. He recorded his first NFL sack against the [[Chicago Bears]] on ''[[NBC Sunday Night Football]]''. Spencer was demoted from his starting position, after Ellis regained his playing form. He finished the season with 28 tackles, 3 sacks, and two forced fumbles.

====2008 season====
Spencer played in just 12 games for the [[2008 Dallas Cowboys season|Cowboys]], starting none. In his limited playing time, Spencer recorded 34 tackles and 1.5 sacks.

====2009 season====
After two years in Dallas's defensive system, he became a starter with the departure of Greg Ellis. He would put together a solid 2009 campaign, recording a career best 67 tackles and 6 sacks, along with 2 forced fumbles and his first career interception. Spencer started all 16 regular season games for the [[2009 Dallas Cowboys season|Cowboys in 2009]], starting at outside linebacker opposite teammate DeMarcus Ware.

While Dallas was able to win their first playoff game in over a decade, the Cowboys fell to the [[2009 Minnesota Vikings season|Minnesota Vikings]] in the NFC Divisional Playoffs. Spencer pitched in two tackles and a sack in the Wild Card game against Philadelphia, and had an outstanding game against the Vikings in the Divisional Round, recording 10 tackles and a sack in a 34-3 Dallas loss.

====2010 season====
Spencer followed up his 2009 season with a very solid 2010 season, as he again started all sixteen games. For the first time in Spencer's Dallas career, the team finished with a losing record, at 6–10 (the Cowboys were 13–3 in 2007, 9–7 in 2008, and 11–5 in 2009). Despite the overall disappointment of [[2010 Dallas Cowboys season|Dallas's season]], Spencer put in a solid 16 starts, recording 63 tackles, 5 sacks, and 2 forced fumbles.

====2011 season====
In the 2011 NFL season (and the last year of Spencer's rookie contract), Spencer recorded 51 solo tackles, 15 assist tackles, for a total of 66 tackles.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nfl.com/player/anthonyspencer/2495745/profile |title=Anthony Spencer Player Profile at NFL.com |work=NFL.com |access-date=May 1, 2016}}</ref> Spencer also recorded 6 sacks, 1 pass deflection and 4 forced fumbles in 15 starts as the Dallas Cowboys finished the season 8–8 with no playoff appearance.

====2012 season====
On March 5, the Dallas Cowboys placed the franchise tag on Spencer. More than a month later, and just before the [[2012 NFL draft]], He officially signed the franchise tag, guaranteeing him a salary of $8.856 million for the 2012 season.<ref>{{cite web| url=http://www.dallascowboys.com/news/2012/04/23/spencer-officially-signs-franchise-tender |title=Spencer Officially Signs Franchise Tender |publisher=DallasCowboys.com |date=April 23, 2012 |access-date=May 1, 2016}}</ref>

Spencer ended up having a break out season and being named to his first [[Pro Bowl]] as an injury replacement for Green Bay's [[Clay Matthews III|Clay Matthews]]. Even though he missed two games, he recorded his first double-digit sack (11) season, had 27 quarterback hurries, led the Cowboys with 95 tackles, and was the only player in the [[NFL]] with 90+ tackles and 10+ sacks.

====2013 season====
For the second year in a row, the Cowboys put the franchise tag on Spencer.<ref>{{cite web|title=Dallas Cowboys Will Use Franchise Tag on DE Anthony Spencer|url=http://www.sportsmedia101.com/dallascowboys/2013/03/04/dallas-cowboys-will-use-franchise-tag-on-de-anthony-spencer/?doing_wp_cron|access-date=March 6, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131224111936/http://www.sportsmedia101.com/dallascowboys/2013/03/04/dallas-cowboys-will-use-franchise-tag-on-de-anthony-spencer/?doing_wp_cron|archive-date=December 24, 2013|url-status=dead}}</ref> The tender is worth $9.6 million.  Under [[Monte Kiffin]] as new defensive coordinator, both Spencer and [[DeMarcus Ware]] were expected to play as [[defensive end]]s as the team reverted to a [[4–3 defense]]. He missed all of the preseason after a surgical procedure that at the time was said to be for a bone bruise on his left knee. He came back to play against the [[Kansas City Chiefs]] registering 2 tackles and one quarterback hurry. After experiencing pain in his knee following the game, he underwent season-ending [[microfracture surgery]].<ref>{{cite web| url=http://www.espn.com/dallas/nfl/story/_/id/9716021/anthony-spencer-dallas-cowboys-undergo-season-ending-knee-surgery | title=Anthony Spencer to have surgery | access-date=February 19, 2017}}</ref>

====2014 season====
After remaining a [[free agent]] for over a month, Spencer re-signed with the Cowboys with a one-year deal on April 26.<ref>{{cite web|last=Sabin|first=Rainer|title=Dallas Cowboys re-sign free agent DE Anthony Spencer|url=http://sportsday.dallasnews.com/dallas-cowboys/cowboysheadlines/2014/04/26/dallas-cowboys-re-sign-free-agent-de-anthony-spencer |publisher=dallasnews.com|access-date=April 26, 2014}}</ref> Recovering from career threatening knee surgery, there were questions of how much he would play in [[2014 NFL season|2014]]. His recovery ramped up at the end of training camp and was able to come back for the fourth game against the [[New Orleans Saints]].

He was solid against the run and steadily improved as a pass rusher, finishing with 17 quarterback pressures (tied for fourth on the team). In the playoffs against the [[Detroit Lions]] he played a season-high 40 snaps and finished the game with 3 tackles, one sack and forced a fumble in the fourth quarter that would have ended the game, had [[DeMarcus Lawrence]] not fumbled the ball while returning it. In two playoff games he registered a sack and led the team with 7 quarterback pressures.

===New Orleans Saints===
On April 10, 2015, Spencer signed a one-year contract with the [[New Orleans Saints]] as a [[free agent]].<ref>{{cite web|last1=Patra|first1=Kevin|title=Anthony Spencer, New Orleans Saints reach contract|url=https://www.nfl.com/news/anthony-spencer-new-orleans-saints-reach-contract-0ap3000000484710|work=NFL.com|access-date=April 11, 2015}}</ref> During preseason, he was playing [[outside linebacker]] with the first team unit and was expected to replace [[Junior Galette]], but after suffering an injury that kept him out of action since the first preseason game, he was placed on the [[injured reserve list]] on September 1,<ref name="n026">{{cite web | last=Triplett | first=Mike | title=Saints to place DE Spencer on injured reserve | website=ESPN.com | date=2015-09-01 | url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/13558116/new-orleans-saints-place-anthony-spencer-injured-reserve | access-date=2024-10-19}}</ref> before being released on October 20.<ref name="f686">{{cite web | title=New Orleans releases Anthony Spencer from injured reserve | website=NOLA.com | date=2015-06-10 | url=https://www.nola.com/sports/saints/new-orleans-releases-anthony-spencer-from-injured-reserve/article_53e9fff7-8dd2-5f4d-9b9d-11419a756daf.html | access-date=2024-10-19}}</ref>

'''Anthony Newman''' (born November 21, 1965) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[Safety (gridiron football position)|safety]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). Newman played for the [[Los Angeles Rams]] from 1988 to 1994, [[New Orleans Saints]] from 1995 to 1997, and the [[Oakland Raiders]] from 1998 to 1999. He was selected by the Rams in the second round of the [[1988 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=1988 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/1988/draft.htm |access-date=2023-09-24 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> Out of high school, he had the opportunity to play [[Major League Baseball]] but chose instead to attend the [[University of Oregon]].

==Post-NFL career==
After retiring from the NFL, Newman worked with the [[Oregon Sports Network]]. He was a commentator for [[Oregon Ducks football]] games. He worked alongside Joe Giansante color commentating on Oregon Duck football games until the conference expanded to the Pac-12 and launched their own sports network. He also helps coach the Central Catholic High School football team. Newman resides in Oregon with his wife, and his three children.

In 1994 Newman and J.J. Birden created the Anthony Q. Newman Foundation<ref name="Foundation">[http://www.anthonyqnewmanfoundation.org/ Anthony Q. Newman Foundation] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110324075138/http://www.anthonyqnewmanfoundation.org/ |date=March 24, 2011 }}</ref> and began offering free football camps.  These camps are no longer active, but Newman still runs the Anthony Newman Sports Camps that take place in the summer, spring, and winter. In 2019 Newman accepted the defensive coordinator position at Central Catholic H.S. in Portland, Oregon.

Co-defensive coordinator & safeties coach | highlights = * [[Super Bowl]] champion ([[Super Bowl XXXV|XXXV]]) * Consensus [[College Football All-America Team|All-American]] ([[1998 College Football All-America Team|1998]]) * First-team All-American ([[1997 College Football All-America Team|1997]]) * [[Atlantic Coast Conference football individual awards#Defensive Player of the Year|ACC Defensive Player of the Year]] (1998) * [[Atlantic Coast Conference football individual awards|ACC Brian Piccolo Award]] (1998) * 3× First-team [[List of All-Atlantic Coast Conference football teams|All-ACC]] ([[1996 All-Atlantic Coast Conference football team|1996]], [[1997 All-Atlantic Coast Conference football team|1997]], [[1998 All-Atlantic Coast Conference football team|1998]]) * [[Dudley Award]] (1997) * [[Virginia Cavaliers football#Retired jerseys|Virginia Cavaliers Jersey No. 3]] retired | pfr = PoinAn20 | CollegeHOF = 2460 }} '''Anthony Scott Poindexter''' (born July 28, 1976) is an American [[American football|football]] coach and former [[Safety (American and Canadian football position)|safety]], who is the current defensive backs coach and co-defensive coordinator for the Tennessee Volunteers. He is the former safeties coach for the [[Penn State Nittany Lions football|Penn State Nittany Lions]]. He played [[college football]] at [[Virginia Cavaliers football|Virginia]] from 1995 to 1998 for head coach [[George Welsh (American football)|George Welsh]], and earned [[All-American]] honors. He then played in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) for the [[Baltimore Ravens]] and [[Cleveland Browns]] from 1999 to 2001. ==Early life== Poindexter, a native of [[Bedford County, Virginia|Bedford County]], Virginia, attended New London Academy, Forest Middle School, and [[Jefferson Forest High School]] in [[Forest, Virginia]].{{cite web |last1=Feldkamp |first1=Justin |title=Poindexter and Berry Honored by VHSL Hall of Fame |url=https://wset.com/archive/poindexter-and-berry-honored-by-vhsl-hall-of-fame |website=wset.com |date=13 October 2013 |publisher=Sinclair Broadcast Group, Inc. |access-date=23 February 2021}} In middle school, he led his team to an undefeated season as quarterback. In high school, Anthony excelled in football, baseball, and basketball. As quarterback and safety, Poindexter led the Cavaliers to back-to-back Division 3 football championships in 1992 and 1993, defeating [[Matoaca High School]] in both finals.{{cite web |last1=Williams |first1=Jennifer |title=CAV-TO-BE DOMINATES ON DEFENSE |url=https://www.dailypress.com/news/dp-xpm-19940715-1994-07-15-9407150018-story.html |website=dailypress.com |publisher=Daily Press |access-date=25 February 2021}} Poindexter earned first-team all-state honors as a junior and senior. He was selected as the 1993 AP Group AA Player of the Year as a senior. Poindexter was drafted by the [[Miami Marlins|Florida Marlins]] of [[Major League Baseball]] during his senior season of high school.{{cite web |url=http://www.virginiasports.com/sports/m-footbl/spec-rel/071513aac.html |title=Poindexter Named to Virginia High School Hall of Fame |date=July 11, 2013 |publisher=University of Virginia |access-date=14 August 2013}} ==College career== Poindexter accepted an athletic scholarship to attend the University of Virginia and he played safety for coach [[George Welsh (American football)|George Welsh]]'s [[Virginia Cavaliers football]] team from 1995 to 1998. He was compared to NFL players such as [[Ronnie Lott]],{{cite news| url = https://www.washingtonpost.com/archive/sports/1996/09/17/at-virginia-safety-poindexter-records-all-the-greatest-hits/f7de720d-a61e-4839-a4b5-be6954d32729/| title = AT VIRGINIA, SAFETY POINDEXTER RECORDS ALL THE GREATEST HITS - The Washington Post| newspaper = [[The Washington Post]]}} for his hard-hitting style. As a [[Redshirt (college sports)|redshirt]] freshman in 1995, Poindexter teamed with fellow [[defensive back]] Adrian Burnim in one of the most famous plays in Cavalier history as the two stopped [[Florida State Seminoles football|Florida State's]] running back [[Warrick Dunn]] inches from the goal line, defeating the second ranked Seminoles 32-28. In 1996, he made a school record with 98 tackles and as a junior in 1997 he finished with 78.{{Cite web|url=http://www.streakingthelawn.com/2015/6/3/8724825/college-football-hall-of-fame-2016-ballot-anthony-poindexter-virginia|title = Anthony Poindexter named to 2016 CFB HOF Ballot|date = 3 June 2015}} As a junior, Poindexter had the choice between declaring himself for the [[1998 NFL draft]] or staying in college for his senior year. Draft experts projected that he would likely be drafted in the first round, but Poindexter stayed at Virginia for his senior season but watched his draft stock plummet as injuries corrupted his senior season. The Cavaliers were expected to have a very strong team and were ranked as high as the top ten. In the first seven games of the season, Poindexter made 73 tackles, two sacks and three interceptions. In a game against N.C. State in 1998, Poindexter made a tackle on [[wide receiver]] Chris Coleman but he twisted his left leg and tore his ACL and two other ligaments. His season at Virginia was over, and possibly his professional career; he could not participate in the [[NFL Scouting Combine]] or the Virginia Pro Day. Poindexter's No. 3 [UVA] jersey was retired on October 10, 2009.{{cite web |url=http://www.virginiasports.com/sports/m-footbl/mtt/anthony_poindexter_800051.html |title=Anthony Poindexter |publisher=University of Virginia |access-date=14 August 2013}} Poindexter was named to the [[College Football Hall of Fame]] in 2020.{{cite web |title=Anthony Poindexter Named To 2020 Class of College Football Hall of Fame |url=https://virginiasports.com/news/2020/03/11/anthony-poindexter-named-to-2020-class-of-college-football-hall-of-fame/ |website=Virginia Cavaliers Official Athletic Site |date=11 March 2020 |access-date=7 January 2021}} ==Professional career== His chances of getting drafted were slim and depended on the teams doctors' opinions. The [[Baltimore Ravens]] took a chance on Poindexter by drafting him in the seventh round with the 216th overall pick.{{Cite web |title=1999 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/1999/draft.htm |access-date=2023-03-29 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}} In his rookie season, he was placed on the [[Injured Reserve|injured reserve]] list, but he returned for the Ravens' championship season in 2000. He played in 10 games on special teams where he caused one forced fumble. He did not play in [[Super Bowl XXXV]], however. Shortly after the game, he was released, but was picked up by the [[Cleveland Browns]] in June 2001. He was released again in September that same year and never played another NFL game. ==Coaching career== After the end of his NFL career in 2001, Poindexter returned to his alma mater as a graduate assistant. He eventually made his way up the coaching totem pole and was the safeties coach at the end of his tenure at the University of Virginia. In 2014, Poindexter accepted a position at the University of Connecticut as the defensive coordinator/safeties coach. Poindexter was dismissed along with the rest of the defensive coaching staff at the end of the 2016 season.{{Cite web|url=https://www.si.com/college/2016/12/26/bob-diaco-fired-uconn-football-head-coach-search|title=UConn head coach Bob Diaco fired after three seasons|publisher=si.com|author=Staff|date=2016-12-26|access-date=2021-12-06}} In 2017, Poindexter was hired as the co-defensive coordinator (along with Nick Holt) and safeties coach. Purdue made two bowl games in his tenure as defensive coordinator. In 2021, Poindexter was hired as safeties coach at Penn State. At the end of the 2023 regular season, PSU defensive coordinator, Manny Diaz, left to take the head coaching position at Duke. Poindexter was then appointed as interim co-defensive coordinator for Penn State's appearance in the Peach Bowl. == References == {{reflist}} ==External links== * {{College Football HoF|2460}} * [https://gopsusports.com/staff/anthony-poindexter Penn State profile] {{Atlantic Coast Conference football Player of the Year navbox}} {{Dudley Award}} {{1998 NCAA Division I-A College Football Consensus All-Americans}} {{Ravens1999DraftPicks}} {{Super Bowl XXXV}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Poindexter, Anthony}} [[Category:1976 births]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:American football safeties]] [[Category:Baltimore Ravens players]] [[Category:Cleveland Browns players]] [[Category:Penn State Nittany Lions coaches]] [[Category:Purdue Boilermakers football coaches]] [[Category:Virginia Cavaliers football coaches]] [[Category:Virginia Cavaliers football players]] [[Category:UConn Huskies football coaches]] [[Category:All-American college football players]] [[Category:College Football Hall of Fame inductees]] [[Category:People from Forest, Virginia]] [[Category:Players of American football from Lynchburg, Virginia]] [[Category:Coaches of American football from Virginia]] [[Category:African-American coaches of American football]]

'''Anthony Eugene Morgan''' (born November 15, 1967) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[wide receiver]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Tennessee Volunteers football|Tennessee Volunteers]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Simeone |first=Matt |date=July 19, 2013 |title=Ex-Bears receiver Morgan a spokesman for Play 60 campaign |url=https://www.chicagobears.com/news/ex-bears-receiver-morgan-a-spokesman-for-play-60-campaign-10495391 |access-date=2024-03-16 |website=Chicago Bears |language=en-US}}</ref> Morgan played six seasons in the NFL for the [[Chicago Bears]] (1991–1993) and the [[Green Bay Packers]] (1993–1996). He was selected by the Bears in the fifth round of the [[1991 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=1991 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/1991/draft.htm |access-date=2023-05-07 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> He is perhaps best known for his performance versus Detroit during the 1994 season, in which he hauled in 6 passes for 103 yards and two touchdowns <ref>{{Cite web |title=Anthony Morgan Career Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/M/MorgAn00/gamelog// |access-date=2024-03-16 |website=[[Pro-Football-Reference.com]]}}</ref>

After his playing career ended, in September 1998, Morgan joined the Christian Valley Missionary Baptist Church and became an [[ordained minister]] in 2006. In July 2012, Morgan became the wide receivers coach at [[Trinity International University]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Mayer|first=Larry|url=http://www.chicagobears.com/news/article-1/Ex-Bears-receiver-Morgan-a-spokesman-for-Play-60-campaign/34f69e63-da17-4ad2-b447-54135afc8ccd|title=Ex-Bears receiver Morgan a spokesman for Play 60 campaign|publisher=[[Chicago Bears]]|date=July 19, 2013|accessdate=July 19, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130723023610/http://www.chicagobears.com/news/article-1/Ex-Bears-receiver-Morgan-a-spokesman-for-Play-60-campaign/34f69e63-da17-4ad2-b447-54135afc8ccd|archive-date=July 23, 2013|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Special teams coordinator & assistant head coach | highlights = * [[National Football League Rookie of the Year Award|NFL Offensive Rookie of the Year]] (2001) * [[PFWA All-Rookie Team]] ([[PFWA All-Rookie Team#2001|2001]]) * [[College football national championships in NCAA Division I FBS|National champion]] ([[1997 Michigan Wolverines football team|1997]]) * Third-team [[College Football All-America Team|All-American]] ([[2000 College Football All-America Team|2000]]) * First-team [[List of All-Big Ten Conference football teams|All-Big Ten]] ([[2000 All-Big Ten Conference football team|2000]]) * Second-team All-Big Ten ([[1999 All-Big Ten Conference football team|1999]]) * [[Big Ten Freshman of the Year]] (1997) | statlabel1 = [[Rushing yards]] | statvalue1 = 3,891 | statlabel2 = [[Average|Rushing average]] | statvalue2 = 3.7 | statlabel3 = [[Touchdown|Rushing Touchdowns]] | statvalue3 = 23 | statlabel4 = [[Reception (gridiron football)|Receptions]] | statvalue4 = 113 | statlabel5 = [[Receiving yards]] | statvalue5 = 756 | statlabel6 = [[Touchdown|Receiving touchdowns]] | statvalue6 = 1 | pfr = ThomAn01 }} '''Anthony''' "'''A-Train'''"{{Cite news |last=Isaacson |first=Melissa |date=January 16, 2002 |title=Rookie award goes to A-Train |url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/2002/01/16/rookie-award-goes-to-a-train/ |access-date=August 29, 2018 |work=Chicago Tribune}} '''Thomas''' (born November 7, 1977) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[running back]] for seven seasons in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Michigan Wolverines football|Michigan Wolverines]] from 1997 to 2000, breaking their career rushing record at the time with a four-year total of 4,472 yards. As a senior he rushed for 1,733 yards with 18 touchdowns, and was selected as a [[2000 All-Big Ten Conference football team|first-team All-Big Ten]] running back. Thomas was selected by the [[Chicago Bears]] in the second round of the [[2001 NFL draft]]. As a rookie with the Bears in 2001, he rushed for over 1,100 yards and seven touchdowns to earn NFL Offensive Rookie of the Year honors. He played for the Bears from 2001 to 2004, [[Dallas Cowboys]] in 2005, [[New Orleans Saints]] in 2005, and [[Buffalo Bills]] from 2006 to 2007. ==Early life== Thomas was born in [[Pineville, Louisiana]], in 1977 and attended Winnfield Senior High School in [[Winnfield, Louisiana]].{{Cite web |title=Anthony Thomas |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/T/ThomAn01.htm |access-date=December 3, 2015 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |publisher=Sports Reference LLC}} He starred on the [[basketball]], [[Track and field athletics|track]], and [[high school football|football]] teams. He totaled 7,594 rushing yards and scored 682 points for the Winnfield tigers. He also set a state record with 106 career [[touchdowns]] while playing both running back and [[placekicker]].{{Cite web |date=January 14, 2013 |title='Take the A-Train': Anthony Thomas' tracks took him from player to coach |url=http://archive.thetowntalk.com/article/20130114/SPORTS30/130114004/-Take-Train-Anthony-Thomas-tracks-took-him-from-player-coach |publisher=thetowntalk.com (a Gannett Company)}}{{dead link|date=August 2017|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}} He was named a first-team [[All-America]]n and rated as the second-best running back in the country by the ''Prep Football Report''. ==College career== Thomas enrolled at the [[University of Michigan]] in 1997. While playing at Michigan, he was given the nickname "A-Train" by [[Brent Musburger]].{{Cite book |last=Angelique Chengelis |title=100 Things Michigan Fans Should Know & Do Before They Die |publisher=Triumph Books |year=2012 |isbn=978-1623680701}} As a freshman, he was a member of the undefeated, national champion [[1997 Michigan Wolverines football team]]. That year, he was the Wolverines' #2 running back (behind [[Chris Howard (American football)|Chris Howard]]), twice rushed for over 100 yards (122 yards against Baylor and 129 yards against Iowa), and compiled a total of 549 rushing yards and 219 receiving yards. He was honored as the [[Big Ten Conference football individual honors#Freshman of the Year|1997 Big Ten Freshman Of the Year]] by both the conference coaches and media. After his freshman year, Thomas led the Wolverines in rushing for three consecutive years with 893 yards in 1998, 1,297 yards in 1999, and 1,733 yards in 2000. His 1,733 rushing yards in 2000 remains the second highest single-season total in Michigan history. During the 2000 season, Thomas had nine games in which he rushed for over 100 yards, including 228 yards against Illinois, 199 yards against Northwestern, and 182 yards against both [[2000 UCLA Bruins football team|UCLA]] and [[2000 Auburn Tigers football team|Auburn]]. He was selected as a second-team [[List of All-Big Ten Conference football teams|All-Big Ten]] player in 1999 (coaches and media),{{Cite web |date=November 30, 1999 |title=Renes, Hutchinson Earn All-Big Ten First Team "Double" |url=http://www.mgoblue.com/sports/m-footbl/spec-rel/113099aab.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151208052737/http://www.mgoblue.com/sports/m-footbl/spec-rel/113099aab.html |archive-date=December 8, 2015 |access-date=December 4, 2015 |website=Mgoblue.com |publisher=University of Michigan}} and as a first-team All-Big Ten player in 2000 (coaches and media). He was also selected as both a team captain and most valuable player on the [[2000 Michigan Wolverines football team|2000 Michigan team]]. Thomas's 4,472 rushing yards broke [[Jamie Morris]]' Michigan career rushing records. (Thomas's record was later broken by [[Mike Hart (American football)|Mike Hart]].) He also broke [[Tyrone Wheatley]]'s modern Michigan career record with 56 touchdowns (Thomas's record was later broken by [[Blake Corum]].) He also set and continues to hold Michigan records with an average of 144.4 rushing yards per game in 2000 and six games in a season with at least 150 rushing yards.{{Cite magazine |last=Austin Murphy |date=October 30, 2000 |title=A-Train Keeps on Chugging Laconic back Anthony Thomas is on track to rewrite Michigan's record book |url=https://www.si.com/vault/2000/10/30/291230/a-train-keeps-on-chugging-laconic-back-anthony-thomas-is-on-track-to-rewrite-michigans-record-book |magazine=Sports Illustrated}} ==Professional career== In April 2001, Thomas was selected by the [[Chicago Bears]] in the second round (38th overall pick) of the [[2001 NFL draft]].{{Cite web |title=2001 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2001/draft.htm |access-date=March 18, 2023 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}} On October 21, 2001, Thomas set two Bears rookie records with 188 rushing yards and a 8.55 yards/carry average in a 24–0 victory over the [[Cincinnati Bengals]].{{Cite news |date=October 22, 2001 |title=Bears Break Out |url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/3765106/bears_break_out/ |work=The Salina Journal |page=16}} He set his third franchise rookie record in the season finale with 33 carries; he also had 160 yards and a touchdown in the clinching victory over [[Jacksonville Jaguars|Jacksonville]]. With 1,183 rushing yards during the [[2001 Chicago Bears season|2001 season]], Thomas helped lead the Bears to a 13–3 record and an NFC Central championship. In January 2002, he received the [[National Football League Rookie of the Year Award#Offensive ROTY winners (1967–present)|AP NFL Offensive Rookie of the Year]] for the 2001 season.{{Cite news |last=Barry Wilner |date=January 16, 2002 |title=A-Train is top offensive rookie: Bears RB Thomas significant factor in team's turnaround |url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/3765147/a_train_is_top_offensive_rookie/ |work=The Salina Journal |page=23}} Thomas remained the Bears' top running back for two more years with 721 rushing yards in 2002 and 1,024 rushing yards in 2003.{{Cite web |title=2002 Chicago Bears |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/teams/chi/2002.htm |access-date=December 4, 2015 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |publisher=Sports Reference LLC}}{{Cite web |title=2003 Chicago Bears |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/teams/chi/2003.htm |access-date=December 4, 2015 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |publisher=Sports Reference LLC}} In 2004, [[Thomas Jones (American football)|Thomas Jones]] took over as the Bears' lead back, and Thomas was limited to 404 yards on 122 carries.{{Cite web |title=2004 Chicago Bears |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/teams/chi/2004.htm |access-date=December 4, 2015 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |publisher=Sports Reference LLC}} In May 2005, Thomas signed a one-year contract with the [[Dallas Cowboys]] and was expected to be the backup running back to [[Julius Jones (American football)|Julius Jones]].{{Cite news |date=May 3, 2005 |title=Transactions – Football |url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/3765177/transactions_football/ |work=Salina Journal |page=12}} He appeared in six games, two as a starter, for the 2005 Cowboys, gaining only 80 yards on 36 carries. Thomas' ineffectiveness in limited duty, his inability to play special teams, and the emergence of [[Marion Barber III]] as the primary backup led Dallas to release him in November 2005. He was quickly signed by [[New Orleans Saints|New Orleans]] after they lost [[Deuce McAllister]] with a season ending knee injury.{{Cite news |date=November 9, 2005 |title=Saints sign veteran Thomas |url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/3765197/saints_sign_veteran_thomas/ |work=Salina Journal |page=14}} Thomas appeared in only four games, all as a backup for the Saints, and gained 12 yards on seven carries. On April 28, 2006, Thomas signed with the [[Buffalo Bills]].{{Cite news |date=April 30, 2006 |title=Transactions – Football |url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/3765229/transactions_football/ |work=The Hays Daily News |page=16}} In 2006, he appeared in 16 games, two as a starter, for the Bills, and gained 378 yards on 107 carries. The following year, he appeared in 10 games and gained 89 yards on 36 carries. He was placed on injured reserve in early December 2007.{{Cite news |date=December 7, 2007 |title=Transactions – Football |url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/3765244/transactions_football/ |work=Aiken Standard |page=4B}} == NFL career statistics == {| class="wikitable" style="text-align:center;" ! rowspan="2" |Year ! rowspan="2" |Team ! colspan="2" |Games ! colspan="5" |Rushing ! colspan="5" |Receiving |- ! '''Anthony Maurice Mitchell''' (born December 13, 1974) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[Safety (American football position)|safety]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Tuskegee Golden Tigers football|Tuskegee Golden Tigers]] and was signed by the [[Baltimore Ravens]] as an [[undrafted free agent]] in 1999.

==Professional career==
Mitchell was originally signed as an undrafted rookie by the [[Jacksonville Jaguars]] in 1999,<ref>{{cite web |title=Transactions |url=https://www.nfl.com/transactions/league/signings/1999/4?after=AAAHzwAAAAQAAAAaAAAAAAAELSQ= |website=NFL.com |access-date=1 August 2024}}</ref> but after the preseason, he was waived in the final cuts. He spent most of the 1999 season on the [[Baltimore Ravens]]' practice squad and was elevated to the 53-man roster for the final four games.<ref>{{cite web |title=Jaguars make moves |url=https://www.jaguars.com/news/jaguars-make-moves-5847902 |website=jaguars.com |access-date=26 August 2003}}</ref> 

Mitchell is best remembered for his play as a reserve safety on the 2000 Ravens squad that made an improbable run to Super Bowl XXXV. In a pivotal January 2001 playoff game played in Nashville, Baltimore was tied 10–10 with the [[Tennessee Titans]] early in the fourth quarter.  With just over 12 minutes remaining in the game, Titans kicker [[Al Del Greco]] lined up for a potential game-winning 37-yard field goal from the right hash.  At the snap, Baltimore defensive lineman [[Keith Washington (American football)|Keith Washington]] bullrushed the Titans lineman defending him, losing his helmet in the process; undeterred, Washington stretched out his right arm over his head, deflecting Del Greco's kick high into the air. Mitchell snatched the tipped ball out of the air at the Ravens' 10-yard line, raced up the far sideline and, with the help of blocks thrown by backup safety [[Corey Harris (American football)|Corey Harris]] and starting cornerback [[Chris McAlister]], returned the ball 90 yards for a Baltimore touchdown.<ref name="ProRef">{{cite web | url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200101070oti.htm | title=Divisional Round - Baltimore Ravens at Tennessee Titans - January 7th, 2001 | website=pro-football-reference.com | access-date=August 7, 2025}}</ref> Mitchell's return catapulted the Ravens to a 24–10 win and set them on the path to their first world championship.<ref name=return_2001>{{cite web|title=Ravens Win Clash With Titans|url=https://www.cbsnews.com/news/ravens-win-clash-with-titans/|agency=[[Associated Press]]|work=[[CBS Sports]]|date=January 7, 2001 |access-date=27 September 2011}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Super Bowl XXXV - Baltimore Ravens vs. New York Giants - January 28th, 2001 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200101280nyg.htm |access-date=2023-03-28 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> 

In 2003, the Jaguars acquired Mitchell from the Ravens in a trade for a conditional draft choice. After playing one season with the Jaguars, Mitchell spent his final three seasons with the [[Cincinnati Bengals]].

'''Anthony Wayne Smith''' (born June 28, 1967) is an American former professional [[National Football League|NFL]] [[American football|football]] player and convicted [[serial killer]]. He was selected by the Raiders 11th overall in the [[1990 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=1990 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/1990/draft.htm |access-date=2023-05-24 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> He played [[college football]] in [[Arizona Wildcats football|Arizona]] and [[Alabama Crimson Tide football|Alabama]].

After retiring from professional sports, Smith was convicted of multiple murders, including the 1999 kidnappings and killings of brothers Kevin and Ricky Nettles and the 2001 torture-murder of Dennis Henderson. In 2016, he was sentenced to three consecutive life terms without the possibility of parole.

==NFL career==
Smith was a [[defensive end]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). On August 29, 1990, during practice, Smith tore the [[medial collateral ligament]] and [[cartilage]] in his right knee, causing him to miss his entire rookie season.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-1990-08-31-sp-273-story.html | title=Raider Top Draft Pick Smith is Sidelined by Knee Injury | website=[[Los Angeles Times]] | date=August 31, 1990 }}</ref>

Following Smith's third season, he signed a four-year contract extension with the Raiders for $7.6 million. In 1997, he opted out of his contract and left the NFL following a brief practice stint with the [[Denver Broncos]].<ref name="Nov2015Conviction">Veronica Rocha, [http://www.latimes.com/local/lanow/la-me-ln--raiders-anthony-wayne-smith-convicted-20151105-story.html Former Raiders player Anthony Wayne Smith convicted in 3 murders], ''Los Angeles Times'' (November 5, 2015).</ref>

==Marriages==
Smith has been married three times. His second wife was former singer–actress Denise Matthews, better known as [[Vanity (singer)|Vanity]].<ref name="Ebony">{{cite journal |date=June 1995 |title=At Home With Vanity And Her New Husband |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=Jd-pEXo2P7UC&dq=ebony&q=vanity#v=snippet&q=vanity&f=false |journal=Ebony |volume=50 |issue=8 |pages=54–58}}</ref> The marriage lasted for a year, from 1995 to 1996.<ref name="Ebony" /> In 1997, Smith was arrested for [[domestic violence]] involving another woman and sentenced to anger-management classes. In 1997, he met his third wife, Teresa Obello White.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Dobie |first=Kathy |date=January 23, 2013 |title=Ex-Raider Anthony Smith's Murder Trial and Violent Past |url=https://www.gq.com/story/nfl-anthony-smith-oakland-raiders-murder |website=GQ}}</ref>

== Firebombing charge ==
In 2003, Smith was charged with [[firebombing]] a [[Santa Monica, California]], furniture store over a dispute with the store's owner about money and a consignment item.<ref name="Nov2015Conviction"/> After two juries were unable to reach a verdict, a judge dismissed the charge.<ref name="Nov2015Conviction"/>

== Murders, trials, and convictions ==
In March 2011, Smith and two others were charged with the murder of Maurilio Ponce, a mechanic, who was beaten and shot in October 2008 in [[Lancaster, California]], with his body dumped near the Antelope Valley poppy fields some 11 miles away.<ref>[http://www.espn.com/nfl/news/story?id=6183025 Anthony Smith charged with murder], Associated Press (March 5, 2011).</ref> Prosecutors said that the murder occurred after a business deal went wrong.<ref name="AP">{{cite web|title=Ex-Raider Ordered to Stand Trial for 4 Murders|url=http://bigstory.ap.org/article/ex-raider-ordered-stand-trial-4-murders|agency=Associated Press|date=October 13, 2012}}</ref>

In April 2011, the jury deadlocked at 8–4 in favor of guilt.<ref name="AP"/> In July 2012, while awaiting retrial, Smith was charged with three other killings: the 1999 murders of brothers Kevin and Ricky Nettles, who were kidnapped from a Los Angeles car wash before being shot and their bodies dumped, and the kidnapping and fatal stabbing of Dennis Henderson in Los Angeles in June 2001.<ref name="AP"/>

On October 12, 2012, after a [[preliminary hearing]], a [[Los Angeles County, California|Los Angeles County]] judge found sufficient evidence for Smith to stand trial for the four murders.<ref name="AP"/> According to testimony at trial, Smith impersonated a police detective while abducting the Nettles, who were [[torture]]d before their murder.<ref>Ann M. Simmons, [https://www.latimes.com/sports/la-xpm-2012-oct-14-la-me-raider-hearing-20121014-story.html Details of slayings recalled at football player's hearing], ''Los Angeles Times'' (October 14, 2012).</ref>

On November 5, 2015, after eight days of jury deliberations, Smith was convicted of the murders of Ricky and Kevin Nettles and Henderson. The jury found special circumstance — "that Smith committed kidnapping, torture, and multiple murders."<ref name="Nov2015Conviction"/> The jury deadlocked 9–3 in favor of guilt on the murder of Ponce.<ref name="Nov2015Conviction"/>

On January 22, 2016, Smith was sentenced to three consecutive life sentences without the possibility of parole.<ref>Veronica Rocha, [http://www.latimes.com/local/lanow/la-me-ln-former-raiders-sentenced-murders-20160122-story.html Former Raiders player Anthony Wayne Smith sentenced to 3 life terms for murders], ''Los Angeles Times'' (January 22, 2016).</ref>

'''Robert Anthony McCoy''' (born December 28, 1987) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[tight end]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[USC Trojans football|USC Trojans]] and was selected by the [[Seattle Seahawks]] in the sixth round of the [[2010 NFL draft]].

==Early life==
McCoy attended [[Bullard High School (Fresno, California)|Bullard High School]] in [[Fresno, California]]. As a senior, he had 70 receptions for 1,210 yards and 15 [[touchdown]]s as a tight end and [[wide receiver]] and 65 [[Tackle (football move)|tackles]] and 14 [[Quarterback sack|sacks]] as [[defensive lineman]].

==College career==
As a freshman in 2006, McCoy played in only four games due to an injury and did not have a reception. As a sophomore in 2007 he played in all 13 games as a backup tight end and on [[special teams]]. He finished the season with two receptions for 18 yards and a touchdown. As a junior in 2008, McCoy started all 13 games at tight end, making 22 receptions for 256 yards and a touchdown.

During his senior year in 2009, McCoy started all 10 games for USC. He missed two games due to nagging injuries, and was named academically ineligible during the season finale against [[Boston College]] in the [[Emerald Bowl]]. McCoy finished the season with 22 catches for 457 yards and one touchdown. His most productive performance of his senior year came in the game against rival [[University of Notre Dame|Notre Dame]], catching 5 passes for 153 yards. McCoy left USC with 46 career catches, 731 career yards, and three career touchdowns.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Anthony McCoy stats |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/player/_/id/13414/anthony-mccoy |access-date=June 17, 2013 |website=ESPN.com}}</ref>

===Seattle Seahawks (first stint)===
McCoy was considered one of the top tight end prospects for the [[2010 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Anthony McCoy, Southern Cal, TE : 2010 NFL Draft Scout Player Profile |url=http://www.nfldraftscout.com/ratings/dsprofile.php?pyid=65845&draftyear=2010&genpos=TENFL |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120312103048/http://www.nfldraftscout.com/ratings/dsprofile.php?pyid=65845&draftyear=2010&genpos=TENFL |archive-date=March 12, 2012 |access-date=June 17, 2013 |website=NFLDraftScout.com}}</ref> He ended up being selected in the sixth round, 185th overall, by the [[Seattle Seahawks]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=2010 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2010/draft.htm |access-date=2023-05-13 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> The move reunited him with his college head coach from USC [[Pete Carroll]] who in 2010 took the head coaching job with Seattle.

On May 21, 2013, McCoy suffered a torn Achilles' during organized team activities, and underwent surgery three days later. His recovery was expected to take about six to nine months, prompting the Seahawks to waive him injured on May 28. After clearing waivers the following day, McCoy reverted to the reserve/injured list.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Anthony McCoy NFL Football player profile |url=http://fantasynews.cbssports.com/fantasyfootball/players/playerpage/1117497/anthony-mccoy |access-date=June 17, 2013 |website=CBSSports.com}}</ref>

On July 29, 2014, McCoy suffered another torn Achilles' during training camp, his second in just over a year. The injury resulted in him missing the entire season and postseason.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Rosenthal |first=Gregg |date=July 29, 2014 |title=Seahawks' Anthony McCoy tears Achilles tendon |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/seahawks-anthony-mccoy-tears-achilles-tendon-0ap2000000371103 |access-date=September 7, 2015 |website=NFL.com}}</ref>

On September 5, 2015, as part of the cutdown to a 53-man roster, the Seahawks terminated McCoy's contract.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Drovetto |first=Tony |date=September 5, 2015 |title=Seahawks Set 53-Man Roster, Trade For Safety Kelcie McCray |url=http://www.seahawks.com/news/2015/09/05/seahawks-set-53-man-roster-trade-safety-kelcie-mccray |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170607232741/http://www.seahawks.com/news/2015/09/05/seahawks-set-53-man-roster-trade-safety-kelcie-mccray |archive-date=June 7, 2017 |access-date=September 7, 2015 |website=Seahawks.com}}</ref>

==Domestic Violence==
In November 2013, Orange was arrested for felony domestic assault by strangulation.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|author1=Michael Martinez |author2= Priscilla Riojas|title=NFL's past penalties for domestic violence|url=https://www.cnn.com/2014/09/09/us/nfl-players-domestic-violence-accusations/index.html|access-date=2020-06-23|website=CNN}}</ref> Police were called to his home early in the morning after Orange reportedly strangled his girlfriend and subsequently threw her on the floor while yelling that she had ignored his text messages.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Stromberg|first=Joseph|date=2014-09-09|title=Ray Rice was indefinitely suspended. Why weren't these players?|url=https://www.vox.com/2014/9/9/6127767/ray-rice-nfl-domestic-violence|access-date=2020-06-23|website=Vox|language=en}}</ref> Orange pleaded guilty to misdemeanor domestic assault and was sentenced to 90 days in jail, reduced to 3 days time served.<ref name=":0" /> Orange was released by the Minnesota Vikings on the day of his arrest but was signed by the Seattle Seahawks in May 2014 following his guilty plea.<ref name=":0" />

'''Anthony Michael Sherman'''<ref name="ProFootballReference.com">{{Cite web |title=Anthony Sherman Stats, Height, Weight, Position, Draft, College |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/S/SherAn00.htm |access-date=2023-02-24 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |archive-date=April 13, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190413043506/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/S/SherAn00.htm |url-status=live }}</ref> (born December 11, 1988) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[fullback (American football)|fullback]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL), primarily with the [[Kansas City Chiefs]]. He played [[college football]] for the [[UConn Huskies football|UConn Huskies]] and was selected by the [[Arizona Cardinals]] in the fifth round of the [[2011 NFL draft]]. His nickname is "'''Sausage'''".<ref>{{Cite web |date=October 12, 2018 |title=All about KC Chiefs fullback Anthony Sherman, aka "Sausage" |url=https://www.kansascity.com/sports/nfl/kansas-city-chiefs/article219940760.html |access-date=2023-02-24 |website=KansasCity.com |archive-date=November 13, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201113100635/https://www.kansascity.com/sports/nfl/kansas-city-chiefs/article219940760.html |url-status=live }}</ref>

==Early life==
Sherman attended [[North Attleboro High School]] in [[North Attleboro, Massachusetts]], where he was the team captain in [[high school football|football]], track, and baseball.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Ventura |first=Danny |date=September 16, 2012 |title=A look back at former North Attleboro star Anthony Sherman, now a member of the Arizona Cardinals |url=http://www.bostonherald.com/sports/high_school/high_school_insider/2012/09/look_back_former_north_attleboro_star_anthony_sherman |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180708075556/http://www.bostonherald.com/sports/high_school/high_school_insider/2012/09/look_back_former_north_attleboro_star_anthony_sherman |archive-date=July 8, 2018 |access-date=April 1, 2018 |website=Boston Herald |language=en}}</ref> He was named the Massachusetts Gatorade Player of the Year in 2006. He was named thrice to the Attleboro Sun-Chronicle All-Star team. In [[high school football|football]], he rushed for 1,202 yards and 20 [[touchdowns]] as a senior, while also adding 100 tackles on defense. He is the school's career leader in rushing yards (2,537) and touchdowns (48).<ref>{{Cite web |date=November 27, 2014 |title=Chiefs' hard-working fullback Anthony Sherman is living the dream |url=http://www.kansascity.com/sports/nfl/kansas-city-chiefs/article4178248.html |access-date=April 1, 2018 |website=Kansas City Chiefs |language=en |archive-date=January 17, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190117054012/https://www.kansascity.com/sports/nfl/kansas-city-chiefs/article4178248.html |url-status=live }}</ref> In [[baseball]], he was a two-time All-League selection.

In [[track & field]], Sherman served as the team captain and competed in the sprinting and throwing events. In sprints, he recorded times of 6.98 seconds in the [[55 meters|55-meter dash]] and 12.19 seconds in the [[100 meters|100-meter dash]]. As a thrower, he competed in the [[shot put]] and got a top-throw of 15.48 meters.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Anthony Sherman |url=https://www.trackingfootball.com/players/anthony-sherman-5209/ |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304024837/https://www.trackingfootball.com/players/anthony-sherman-5209/ |archive-date=March 4, 2016 |website=Tracking Football}}</ref>

Coming out of high school, Sherman was rated a 3-star recruit by Rivals and 247 Sports. He received only two Division 1 scholarship offers, from [[UConn Huskies football|UConn]] and [[Boston College Eagles football|Boston College]]. He ultimately decided to commit to play for the [[University of Connecticut]] on February 7, 2007.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Anthony Sherman, North Attleboro, Inside Linebacker |url=https://247sports.com/Player/Anthony-Sherman-53728/?PlayerInstitution=92009 |access-date=October 3, 2018 |website=247Sports |language=en-US |archive-date=May 19, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180519042633/https://247sports.com/Player/Anthony-Sherman-53728?PlayerInstitution=92009 |url-status=live }}</ref>

==College career==
As a freshman in 2007, Sherman immediately became the starting fullback for the UConn Huskies and was the lead blocker for [[Donald Brown (running back)|Donald Brown]], the 2008 [[Big East Offensive Player of the Year]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Anthony Sherman 2007 Game Log |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/anthony-sherman-1/gamelog/2007/ |access-date=April 1, 2018 |language=en |archive-date=April 2, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180402035748/https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/anthony-sherman-1/gamelog/2007/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

As a sophomore in 2008, Sherman had his best year statistically. He had three carries for 9 yards, had 26 receptions for 270 yards, and 13 tackles on special teams.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Anthony Sherman 2008 Game Log |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/anthony-sherman-1/gamelog/2008/ |access-date=April 1, 2018 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en |archive-date=April 2, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180402035448/https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/anthony-sherman-1/gamelog/2008/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

In his junior and senior seasons, Sherman was elected team captain and was the lead blocker for fellow Massachusetts native, [[Jordan Todman]], who was the 2010 [[Big East Offensive Player of the Year]] and an ESPN All-American. Sherman scored his first collegiate touchdown during his senior season.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Anthony Sherman 2009 Game Log |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/anthony-sherman-1/gamelog/2009/ |access-date=April 1, 2018 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en |archive-date=April 2, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180402035743/https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/anthony-sherman-1/gamelog/2009/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Anthony Sherman 2010 Game Log |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/anthony-sherman-1/gamelog/2010/ |access-date=April 1, 2018 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en |archive-date=April 2, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180402101149/https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/anthony-sherman-1/gamelog/2010/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

During his collegiate career, Sherman rushed for 61 yards on 17 carries, caught 48 passes for 477 yards and a touchdown, and had 63 total tackles.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Anthony Sherman College Stats, School, Draft, Gamelog, Splits |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/anthony-sherman-1.html |access-date=2023-02-24 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en |archive-date=October 13, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221013132013/https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/anthony-sherman-1.html |url-status=live }}</ref>

===Arizona Cardinals===
Sherman was selected by the [[Arizona Cardinals]] in the fifth round, 136th overall, of the [[2011 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=2011 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2011/draft.htm |access-date=April 1, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |archive-date=March 27, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190327105735/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2011/draft.htm |url-status=live }}</ref> In his rookie season, he had eight receptions for 72 yards.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Anthony Sherman 2011 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/S/SherAn00/gamelog/2011/ |access-date=April 1, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |archive-date=April 2, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180402105719/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/S/SherAn00/gamelog/2011/ |url-status=live }}</ref> In the 2012 season, he had five receptions for 39 yards.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Anthony Sherman 2012 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/S/SherAn00/gamelog/2012/ |access-date=April 1, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |archive-date=April 2, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180402105706/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/S/SherAn00/gamelog/2012/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

===Kansas City Chiefs===
Sherman was traded to the [[Kansas City Chiefs]] on May 1, 2013, in exchange for cornerback [[Javier Arenas (American football)|Javier Arenas]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Yates |first=Field |author-link=Field Yates |date=May 1, 2013 |title=Chiefs deal Javier Arenas to Cards |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/9231948/kansas-city-chiefs-trade-javier-arenas-arizona-cardinals-anthony-sherman |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131029202248/http://espn.go.com/nfl/story/_/id/9231948/kansas-city-chiefs-trade-javier-arenas-arizona-cardinals-anthony-sherman |archive-date=October 29, 2013 |access-date=May 1, 2013 |website=[[ESPN.com]]}}</ref> On October 27, 2013, Sherman caught a touchdown pass from [[Alex Smith]] against the [[2013 Cleveland Browns|Cleveland Browns]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Cleveland Browns at Kansas City Chiefs - October 27th, 2013 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201310270kan.htm |access-date=April 1, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |archive-date=April 2, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180402035616/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201310270kan.htm |url-status=live }}</ref> Overall, he finished the 2013 season with 18 receptions for 155 yards and a touchdown.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Anthony Sherman 2013 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/S/SherAn00/gamelog/2013/ |access-date=April 1, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |archive-date=April 2, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180402035537/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/S/SherAn00/gamelog/2013/ |url-status=live }}</ref> In the [[2013–14 NFL playoffs#AFC: Indianapolis Colts 45, Kansas City Chiefs 44|Wild Card Round]] against the [[2013 Indianapolis Colts season|Indianapolis Colts]], he recorded a five-yard receiving touchdown in the 45–44 loss.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Wild Card - Kansas City Chiefs at Indianapolis Colts - January 4th, 2014 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201401040clt.htm |access-date=2020-09-29 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |archive-date=September 4, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170904065457/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201401040clt.htm |url-status=live }}</ref> Sherman signed a contract extension with the Chiefs on November 5, 2014.<ref>{{Cite web |date=November 5, 2014 |title=Chiefs Sign FB Anthony Sherman to Contract Extension |url=https://www.chiefs.com/news/chiefs-sign-fb-anthony-sherman-to-contract-extension-14168022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200917180609/https://www.chiefs.com/news/chiefs-sign-fb-anthony-sherman-to-contract-extension-14168022 |archive-date=September 17, 2020 |access-date=September 17, 2020 |website=Chiefs.com}}</ref> Overall, he finished the 2014 season with 10 receptions for 71 yards and a touchdown.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Anthony Sherman 2014 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/S/SherAn00/gamelog/2014/ |access-date=April 1, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |archive-date=April 2, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180402035534/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/S/SherAn00/gamelog/2014/ |url-status=live }}</ref>  In the 2015 season, he only had four receptions for 34 yards but did appear in all 16 games.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Anthony Sherman 2015 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/S/SherAn00/gamelog/2015/ |access-date=April 1, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |archive-date=April 2, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180402105708/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/S/SherAn00/gamelog/2015/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

In the 2016 season, Sherman appeared in all 16 games, of which he started three. He totaled  four receptions for 11 yards.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Anthony Sherman 2016 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/S/SherAn00/gamelog/2016/ |access-date=April 1, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |archive-date=April 2, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180402105721/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/S/SherAn00/gamelog/2016/ |url-status=live }}</ref> On September 17, 2017, in Week 2 against the [[2017 Philadelphia Eagles season|Philadelphia Eagles]], he recovered a fumble on a [[Darren Sproles]] punt return.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Philadelphia Eagles at Kansas City Chiefs - September 17th, 2017 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201709170kan.htm |access-date=October 21, 2017 |website=[[Pro-Football-Reference.com]] |archive-date=July 23, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190723203219/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201709170kan.htm |url-status=live }}</ref>  In the last week of the 2017 season, Sherman scored his first rushing touchdown of his NFL career. He scored up the middle against the [[2017 Denver Broncos|Denver Broncos]] on a 14-carry, 40-yard performance.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Kansas City Chiefs at Denver Broncos - December 31st, 2017 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201712310den.htm |access-date=April 1, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |archive-date=January 25, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180125031351/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201712310den.htm |url-status=live }}</ref> Overall, he finished the 2017 season with six receptions for 40 yards in addition to the 14 carries for 40 yards.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Anthony Sherman 2017 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/S/SherAn00/gamelog/2017/ |access-date=April 1, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |archive-date=April 2, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180402105729/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/S/SherAn00/gamelog/2017/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

On March 12, 2018, Sherman signed a one-year contract extension with the Chiefs.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Roesch |first=Wesley |date=March 15, 2018 |title=Anthony Sherman's contract is a one-year deal |url=https://chiefswire.usatoday.com/2018/03/15/anthony-shermans-contract-is-a-one-year-deal/ |access-date=September 17, 2020 |website=USAToday.com |archive-date=October 22, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201022093911/https://chiefswire.usatoday.com/2018/03/15/anthony-shermans-contract-is-a-one-year-deal/ |url-status=live }}</ref> In the Chiefs' 2018 season opener against the [[2018 Los Angeles Chargers|Los Angeles Chargers]], he recorded a 36-yard receiving touchdown in the 38–28 victory.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Oberholtz |first=Chris |last2=Welniak |first2=Dani |date=September 10, 2018 |title=Unsung heroes make big difference in Chiefs win over Chargers |url=https://www.kctv5.com/news/local_news/unsung-heroes-make-big-difference-in-chiefs-win-over-chargers/article_1933de9c-b53e-11e8-9649-873747360250.html |access-date=October 3, 2018 |website=KCTV5 News |language=en |archive-date=October 4, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181004021248/https://www.kctv5.com/news/local_news/unsung-heroes-make-big-difference-in-chiefs-win-over-chargers/article_1933de9c-b53e-11e8-9649-873747360250.html |url-status=live }}</ref>

On March 22, 2019, Sherman signed a one-year $1.02 million contract extension with the Chiefs,<ref>{{Cite web |last=Gantt |first=Darin |date=March 22, 2019 |title=Chiefs bringing back Anthony Sherman |url=https://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2019/03/22/chiefs-bringing-back-anthony-sherman/ |access-date=September 17, 2020 |website=Pro Football Talk |publisher=NBC Sports |archive-date=August 1, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210801151112/https://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2019/03/22/chiefs-bringing-back-anthony-sherman/ |url-status=live }}</ref> and won an NFL championship in [[Super Bowl LIV]] with the team.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Wilner |first=Barry |date=February 2, 2020 |title=Mahomes leads Chiefs' rally past 49ers in Super Bowl, 31-20 |url=https://apnews.com/8f6178fbfa3844677b5fc374bc53b80f |access-date=September 17, 2020 |website=AP News |publisher=The Associated Press |archive-date=August 12, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200812012154/https://apnews.com/8f6178fbfa3844677b5fc374bc53b80f |url-status=live }}</ref>

On April 6, 2020, Sherman signed a one-year contract with the Chiefs.<ref>{{Cite web |date=March 24, 2020 |title=Chiefs' Anthony Sherman: Committed to Kansas City |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/football/news/chiefs-anthony-sherman-committed-to-kansas-city/ |access-date=September 17, 2020 |website=CBSSports.com |archive-date=March 25, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200325064614/https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/football/news/chiefs-anthony-sherman-committed-to-kansas-city/ |url-status=live }}</ref> Following the release of long-time Chiefs punter [[Dustin Colquitt]] in the 2020 offseason, Sherman became tied with [[Travis Kelce]] and [[Eric Fisher (American football)|Eric Fisher]] as the longest tenured members of the Chiefs.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Conner |first=Matt |title=Travis Kelce's growth as a leader now faces new challenge |url=https://arrowheadaddict.com/2020/05/13/travis-kelces-growth-leader-longest-tenured-chiefs/ |access-date=September 17, 2020 |website=Arrowhead Addict |date=May 13, 2020 |archive-date=August 20, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200820124715/https://arrowheadaddict.com/2020/05/13/travis-kelces-growth-leader-longest-tenured-chiefs/ |url-status=live }}</ref> On October 13, 2020, he was placed on the reserve/[[COVID-19]] list after being exposed to someone who tested positive for [[COVID-19]]. He would eventually test positive himself.<ref>{{Cite web |date=October 14, 2020 |title=Reports: Kansas City Chiefs fullback Anthony Sherman added to COVID-19 reserve list |url=https://www.kmbc.com/article/reports-kansas-city-chiefs-fullback-anthony-sherman-added-to-covid-19-reserve-list/34362807 |access-date=2023-02-24 |website=KMBC.com |archive-date=October 14, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201014034100/https://www.kmbc.com/article/reports-kansas-city-chiefs-fullback-anthony-sherman-added-to-covid-19-reserve-list/34362807 |url-status=live }}</ref> He was activated on November 4.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Goldman |first=Charles |date=November 4, 2020 |title=Chiefs activate FB Anthony Sherman from reserve/COVID-19 list |url=https://chiefswire.usatoday.com/2020/11/04/kansas-city-chiefs-anthony-sherman-activated-reserve-covid-19-list/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201130054310/https://chiefswire.usatoday.com/2020/11/04/kansas-city-chiefs-anthony-sherman-activated-reserve-covid-19-list/ |archive-date=November 30, 2020 |access-date=December 6, 2020 |website=Chiefs Wire|publisher=USA Today}}</ref>

===Controversy===
When speaking on the NFL's requirements for players during the [[2021 NFL season|2021 season]] for players not vaccinated against [[COVID-19]], Sherman generated controversy. The league had required unvaccinated players to wear a wristband. Those wristbands, Sherman compared to [[Racial segregation in the United States|segregation]] on his Twitter account. He tweeted "The @NFL is making players wear colored wrist bands now based on vaccination status. Funny, I thought we all agreed on the evils of segregation back in the 60s. Here we are again- only this time it’s based on personal health choices instead of skin color". He followed that tweet up with another one saying "The league clearly values being woke, not awake. What a shame. And what a sham". The tweets received primarily mixed reactions.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Reyes |first=Lorenzo |date=July 31, 2021 |title=Retired NFL fullback Anthony Sherman compares COVID-19 vaccination wristbands to racial segregation |url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/nfl/chiefs/2021/07/31/anthony-sherman-likens-covid-19-vaccination-wristbands-segregation/5443149001/ |access-date=2023-02-24 |website=USAToday.com |archive-date=August 26, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210826213735/https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/nfl/chiefs/2021/07/31/anthony-sherman-likens-covid-19-vaccination-wristbands-segregation/5443149001/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

'''Anthony Steen''' (born May 9, 1990) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[Center (gridiron football)|center]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Alabama Crimson Tide football|Alabama Crimson Tide]]. Steen was a member of Alabama's [[2009 Alabama Crimson Tide football team|2009 national championship team]] during his [[Redshirt (college sports)|redshirt]] year as a freshman and played as a starting offensive guard for both the [[2011 Alabama Crimson Tide football team|2011]] and [[2012 Alabama Crimson Tide football team|2012]] national championship teams. After going undrafted in the [[2014 NFL draft]], Steen signed as an undrafted free agent with the [[Arizona Cardinals]].

==Early life==
Steen played [[high school football]] at the [[Clarksdale, Mississippi#Education|Lee Academy]] in [[Clarksdale, Mississippi]], and was a part of the 2009 [[Recruiting (college athletics)|recruiting class]] at Alabama.<ref name="SteenCom">{{Cite news |last=Pillion |first=Dennis |date=July 29, 2008 |title=Steen commits to cap another busy recruiting day |url=http://www.al.com/sports/huntsville/index.ssf/2008/07/steen_commits_to_cap_another_b.html |access-date=July 18, 2013 |publisher=AL.com}}</ref> He verbally committed to the Crimson Tide on July 29, 2008, and officially signed on [[National Signing Day]] the following February.<ref name=SteenCom/> He selected Alabama over offers from [[Florida State Seminoles football|Florida State]], [[Miami Hurricanes football|Miami]], [[Mississippi State Bulldogs football|Mississippi State]], and [[Southern Miss Golden Eagles football|Southern Miss]].<ref name="SteenOffers">{{Cite news |date=July 30, 2008 |title=Alabama picks up two commitments on Tuesday |url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?id=kTgoAAAAIBAJ&sjid=K70EAAAAIBAJ&dq=anthony-steen%20lee-academy&pg=5981%2C6336514 |access-date=July 20, 2010 |work=The Tuscaloosa News}}</ref>

==College career==
[[File:Anthony Steen at Alabama.jpg|thumb|left|Steen with Alabama in 2013]]
After Steen was redshirted for the 2009 season, he started the final two regular season games of the 2010 season after starting guard [[Barrett Jones]] was injured against [[2010 Mississippi State Bulldogs football team|Mississippi State]].<ref name="Steen2010">{{Cite news |last=Chase |first=Goodbread |date=July 29, 2008 |title=After a long absence, Barrett Jones back at practice |url=http://www.tuscaloosanews.com/article/20101218/news/101219602 |access-date=July 18, 2010 |work=The Tuscaloosa News}}</ref>

For the 2011 season, Steen became a starter on the offensive line at the guard position. He played in all 13 games, but only started in 9 after he suffered concussion against [[2011 Ole Miss Rebels football team|Ole Miss]].<ref name="SteenALBio">{{Cite web |title=Anthony Steen bio |url=http://www.rolltide.com/sports/m-footbl/mtt/anthony_steen_449637.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130520064831/http://www.rolltide.com/sports/m-footbl/mtt/anthony_steen_449637.html |archive-date=May 20, 2013 |access-date=July 18, 2013 |publisher=RollTide.com}}</ref><ref name="Steen2011">{{Cite news |last=Aschoff |first=Edward |author-link=Edward Aschoff |date=October 22, 2011 |title=Offensive line changes in Tuscaloosa |url=https://www.espn.com/blog/sec/post/_/id/31104/offensive-line-changes-in-tuscaloosa |access-date=July 18, 2013 |work=ESPN.com}}</ref> For his redshirt junior season in 2012, Steen started all 14 games at the right guard position and was named the team's offensive player of the week for his performance against [[2012 Western Carolina Catamounts football team|Western Carolina]].<ref name=SteenALBio/> At the conclusion of the season, Steen was the only member of the offensive line that did not record a [[Penalty (gridiron football)|penalty]] or allow a [[quarterback sack]] for the season.<ref name="Steen2012">{{Cite news |last=Alex |first=Scarborough |date=April 2, 2013 |title=Quiet period is over |url=https://www.espn.com/colleges/alabama/football/story/_/id/9126181/anthony-steen-quietly-perfect-alabama-crimson-tide-2012 |access-date=July 18, 2013 |work=ESPN.com}}</ref> After the completion of the 2012 season, Steen announced he would return for his senior season.<ref name="SteenRet">{{Cite news |date=January 10, 2013 |title=Anthony Steen to return to Alabama for senior football season |url=http://cw.ua.edu/2013/01/10/anthony-steen-to-return-to-alabama-for-senior-football-season/ |access-date=July 18, 2013 |work=The Crimson White}}</ref> At the time of his announcement Steen cited both to improve his draft stock as well as a desire to compete for one final season at Alabama as his reasons for remaining with the Crimson Tide.<ref name=SteenRet/> For the [[2014 NFL draft]], Steen is ranked as one of the top offensive guards in his class.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2014 Top NFL Draft Prospects: Offensive Guard |url=http://www.cbssports.com/nfl/draft/prospectrankings/2014/OG |access-date=July 18, 2013 |publisher=cbssports.com}}</ref> For his final season at Alabama, Steen and [[Cyrus Kouandjio]] were the only returning starters on the offensive line and both were also named to various award watchlists for the 2013 season.<ref name=Steen2012/>

As the only [[Senior (education)|senior]] on the offensive line for the [[2013 Alabama Crimson Tide football team|2013 season]], Steen was the leader of the line. For his performance against [[2013 Kentucky Wildcats football team|Kentucky]], Steen was recognized as SEC Offensive Linemen of the Week.<ref name="KYPoW">{{Cite news |last=Casagrande |first=Michael |date=October 14, 2013 |title=Alabama OL Anthony Steen honored after historic offensive performance at Kentucky |url=http://www.al.com/alabamafootball/index.ssf/2013/10/alabama_ol_anthony_steen_honor.html |access-date=October 21, 2013 |publisher=AL.com}}</ref>

Steen was a second-team [[List of All-SEC football teams|All-Southeastern Conference]] (SEC) selection.<ref>{{Cite web |date=December 10, 2013 |title=2013 All-SEC Football Team Announced |url=http://www.secdigitalnetwork.com/NEWS/tabid/473/Article/248317/2013-all-sec-football-team-announced.aspx |website=SEC Digital Network}}</ref>
