===Arizona Cardinals===
After going undrafted in the [[2014 NFL draft]], Steen signed with the [[Arizona Cardinals]] as an [[undrafted free agent]] on May 12, 2014.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Urban |first=Darren |date=May 12, 2014 |title=Cardinals Get 15 Undrafted Rookies |url=http://www.azcardinals.com/news-and-events/article-2/Cardinals-Get-15-Undrafted-Rookies/624bb680-e88d-49cf-8aa5-38a70b06986a |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140515021241/http://www.azcardinals.com/news-and-events/article-2/Cardinals-Get-15-Undrafted-Rookies/624bb680-e88d-49cf-8aa5-38a70b06986a |archive-date=May 15, 2014 |access-date=June 1, 2014 |website=AZCardinals.com}}</ref> The Cardinals released Steen on August 30, 2014, but he was re-signed to their practice squad the next day.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Cardinals Cut To 53 |url=http://www.azcardinals.com/news-and-events/article-2/Cardinals-Cut-To-53/552f8ee4-1e2a-4da1-b6a7-3e4f0a52e2d2 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140901194443/http://www.azcardinals.com/news-and-events/article-2/Cardinals-Cut-To-53/552f8ee4-1e2a-4da1-b6a7-3e4f0a52e2d2 |archive-date=September 1, 2014 |access-date=August 31, 2014}}</ref>

On September 5, 2015, he was released by the Cardinals.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Urban |first=Darren |date=September 5, 2015 |title=Cardinals Make Final Roster Cuts |url=http://www.azcardinals.com/news-and-events/article-2/Cardinals-Make-Final-Roster-Cuts/7631774a-731e-47ea-9da7-2b1d0fd86d34 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171107030807/http://www.azcardinals.com/news-and-events/article-2/Cardinals-Make-Final-Roster-Cuts/7631774a-731e-47ea-9da7-2b1d0fd86d34 |archive-date=November 7, 2017 |access-date=September 11, 2015 |website=AZCardinals.com}}</ref> On September 10, 2015, Steen was brought back to the team and was placed on the practice squad. On September 22, 2015, he was released by the Cardinals.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Urban |first=Darren |date=September 22, 2015 |title=Kerwynn Williams cut as Massie returns |url=http://blog.azcardinals.com/2015/09/22/kerwynn-williams-cut-as-massie-returns/ |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151006020111/http://blog.azcardinals.com/2015/09/22/kerwynn-williams-cut-as-massie-returns/ |archive-date=October 6, 2015 |access-date=October 5, 2015 |website=AZCardinals.com}}</ref>

===Miami Dolphins===
On November 24, 2015, Steen was signed to the Dolphins' practice squad.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Warnemuende, Jeremy |date=November 25, 2015 |title=Dolphins sign G Anthony Steen, CB Dax Swanson to practice squad |url=http://mia.247sports.com/Bolt/Dolphins-sign-G-Anthony-Steen-CB-Dax-Swanson-to-practice-squad-41390880 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151128053918/http://mia.247sports.com/Bolt/Dolphins-sign-G-Anthony-Steen-CB-Dax-Swanson-to-practice-squad-41390880 |url-status=dead |archive-date=November 28, 2015 |access-date=May 31, 2017 |website=247Sports.com}}</ref>

Steen made the Dolphins' final roster in 2016, starting seven games at center in place of injured Pro Bowl starter [[Mike Pouncey]].

In 2017, Steen was named the starting left guard to start the season.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Poupart, Alain |date=September 4, 2017 |title=Top News: Steen To Start, Maualuga Update & More |url=http://www.miamidolphins.com/news/article-1/Top-News-Steen-To-Start-Maualuga-Update--More/0a8ec124-8a9b-4bb0-9209-82540e8c9ac8 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170906091601/http://www.miamidolphins.com/news/article-1/Top-News-Steen-To-Start-Maualuga-Update--More/0a8ec124-8a9b-4bb0-9209-82540e8c9ac8 |archive-date=September 6, 2017 |access-date=September 6, 2017 |website=MiamiDolphins.com}}</ref> He started the first six games before being placed on injured reserve on October 31, 2017, with a foot injury.<ref>{{Cite web |date=October 31, 2017 |title=Dolphins Make Roster Moves |url=http://www.miamidolphins.com/news/press-releases/article-1/Dolphins-Make-Roster-Moves/50c12172-7ff1-4ca8-a72f-553cf87998be |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180409072921/http://www.miamidolphins.com/news/press-releases/article-1/Dolphins-Make-Roster-Moves/50c12172-7ff1-4ca8-a72f-553cf87998be |archive-date=April 9, 2018 |website=MiamiDolphins.com}}</ref>

'''Anthony Levala Shelton''' (born September 4, 1967) is an American former professional [[gridiron football|football]] [[defensive back]] who played two seasons with the [[San Diego Chargers]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He was selected by the [[San Francisco 49ers]] in the eleventh round of the [[1990 NFL draft]] after playing [[college football]] at [[Tennessee State University]]. Shelton also played for the [[Winnipeg Blue Bombers]] and [[Shreveport Pirates]] of the [[Canadian Football League]] (CFL).

==Early life and college==
Anthony Levala Shelton was born on September 4, 1967, in [[Fayetteville, Tennessee]].<ref name="Pfa">{{cite web | url=https://profootballarchives.com/players/s/shel02800.html | title=ANTHONY SHELTON | publisher=Pro Football Archives | accessdate=17 April 2025}}</ref> He played [[high school football]] at [[Lincoln County High School (Tennessee)|Lincoln County High School]] in Fayetteville from 1982 to 1984.<ref name="Hs"/><ref name="Pfa"/> Lincoln County High had a 31–5 record during his three seasons there and won the state title in 1982.<ref name="Hs"/> Shelton earned All-District honors as both a junior and senior.<ref name="Hs"/> In 2014, he was inducted into Lincoln County High's Falcon Football Hall of Fame.<ref name="Hs">{{cite news | url=https://www.elkvalleytimes.com/sports/local/eight-inducted-into-falcon-hall-of-fame/article_ed61180e-e3f2-5c0c-9366-7ebe466a7e30.html | title=Eight inducted into Falcon Hall of Fame | work=[[Elk Valley Times]] | date=October 27, 2014 | accessdate=17 April 2025}}</ref>

Shelton played [[college football]] for the [[Tennessee State Tigers football|Tennessee State Tigers]] of [[Tennessee State University]].<ref name="Pfr"/>

==Professional career==
Shelton was selected by the [[San Francisco 49ers]] in the 11th round, with the 289th overall pick, of the [[1990 NFL draft]].<ref name="Pfr">{{cite web | url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/S/ShelAn20.htm | title=Anthony Shelton | publisher=[[Pro Football Reference]] | accessdate=17 April 2025}}</ref> He officially signed with the team on July 26.<ref name="transactions"/> He was waived by the 49ers on September 3, 1990.<ref name="transactions"/>

Shelton was claimed off waivers by the [[San Diego Chargers]] on September 4, 1990.<ref name="transactions"/> He played in 14 games for the Chargers during the 1990 season.<ref name="Pfr"/> He appeared in 11 games, starting four, in 1991, recording one interception and one sack.<ref name="Pfr"/> Shelton was placed on injured reserve on November 30, 1991, due to a sore shoulder.<ref name="transactions"/><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-1991-11-26-sp-66-story.html |title=Chargers' Painful Year Continues to Worsen : Pro football: Seven players might be forced to miss the game Sunday against the Raiders because of injuries. |work=latimes.com |date=November 26, 1991 |access-date=May 2, 2015 |author=McKIibben, Dave |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150502235221/http://articles.latimes.com/1991-11-26/sports/sp-66_1_football-players |archive-date=May 2, 2015 }}</ref> He became a free agent after the 1991 season and re-signed with the team on July 16, 1992.<ref name="transactions"/> He was placed on injured reserve again in August 1992 and missed the entire season.<ref name="transactions"/> Wilson was released by the Chargers on August 24, 1993.<ref name="transactions">{{cite web | url=https://profootballarchives.com/transactions/s/shel02800.html | title=Anthony Shelton Transactions | publisher=Pro Football Archives | accessdate=17 April 2025}}</ref>

Shelton signed with the [[Winnipeg Blue Bombers]] of the [[Canadian Football League]] in May 1994.<ref>{{cite news | url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-leader-post/170560254/ | title=Transactions | work=[[The Leader-Post]] | date=May 30, 1994 | accessdate=17 April 2025 | pages=B8}}</ref> He dressed in five games for the Blue Bombers during the [[1994 CFL season]], totaling nine defensive tackles, seven special teams tackles, one interception, and one pass breakup.<ref name="Pfa"/>

On August 31, 1994, it was reported that Shelton had been "transferred" to the [[Shreveport Pirates]] as part of a "lend-lease program."<ref>{{cite news | url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-kalamazoo-gazette/170564756/ | title=Transactions | work=[[The Kalamazoo Gazette]] | date=August 31, 1994 | accessdate=18 April 2025 | pages=B4}}</ref><ref name="Lease">{{cite news | url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-leader-post/170564786/ | title=Moore playing a waiting game | work=[[The Leader-Post]] | date=December 14, 1994 | accessdate=18 April 2025 | author=Hamilton, Ian | pages=B3}}</ref> He dressed in ten games for the Pirates in 1994, recording 29 defensive tackles, 15 special teams tackles, one interception, and four pass breakups.<ref name="Pfa"/>

After the 1994 season ended, Shelton, who reportedly wanted to stay in Shreveport, was transferred back to the Blue Bombers per the terms of the lend-lease deal.<ref name="Lease"/> He was released by Winnipeg on June 5, 1995.<ref>{{cite news | url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-winnipeg-sun/170565100/ | title=Never let 'em see you sweat, eh, Bob? | work=[[The Winnipeg Sun]] | date=June 6, 1995 | accessdate=18 April 2025 | pages=30}}</ref>

Shelton then signed with the Pirates in June 1995.<ref>{{cite news | url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-times/170565243/ | title=Pirates cut Skaggs, team roster to 65 | work=[[The Times (Shreveport, Louisiana)|The Times]] | date=June 12, 1995 | accessdate=18 April 2025 | pages=1C}}</ref> He dressed in 17 games during the 1995 season, accumulating 64 defensive tackles, ten special teams tackles, two interceptions, two pass breakups, and two sacks.<ref name="Pfa"/> The Pirates folded after the season.

On March 7, 1996, Shelton was selected by the [[Hamilton Tiger-Cats]] with the 115th overall pick of the [[1996 CFL Dispersal Draft]].<ref>{{cite news | url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-hamilton-spectator/170565453/ | title=Winfield, Cats still talking | work=[[The Hamilton Spectator]] | date=March 9, 1996 | accessdate=18 April 2025 | author=Dickins, Jeff | pages=C3}}</ref> He was released by the Tiger-Cats on June 14, 1996.<ref name="transactions"/>

He was selected by the [[New York Giants]] in the ninth round of the [[1992 NFL draft]] after playing [[college football]] at [[Washington State University]]. Prior also played for the [[Calgary Stampeders]] and [[BC Lions]] of the [[Canadian Football League]] (CFL). ==Early life== Anthony Eugene Prior was born on March 27, 1970, in [[Lowell, Massachusetts]].{{cite web | url=https://www.profootballarchives.com/players/p/prio00200.html | title=Anthony Prior | publisher=Pro Football Archives | accessdate=23 December 2024}} He attended [[Rubidoux High School]] in [[Riverside, California]]. ==College career== Prior was a member of the [[Washington State Cougars football|Washington State Cougars]] from 1988 to 1991 and a three-year [[letterman (sports)|letterman]] from 1989 to 1991. He returned two kicks for 23 yards and one punt for 17 yards in 1989.{{cite web | url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/anthony-prior-1.html | title=Anthony Prior | publisher=sports-reference.com | accessdate=23 December 2024}} He returned 20 kicks for 424 yards and a [[Pacific-10 Conference]]-tying one touchdown in 1990. Prior totaled one interception and 22 kick returns for 530 yards and one touchdown his senior year in 1991. His one kick return touchdown was tied for most in the country that season. ==Professional career== Prior was selected by the [[New York Giants]] in the ninth round, with the 238th overall pick, of the [[1992 NFL draft]]. He officially signed with the team on July 21. He was released on August 25, 1992.{{cite web | url=http://www.profootballarchives.com/transactions/p/prio00200.html | title=Anthony Prior NFL Transactions | publisher=Pro Football Archives | accessdate=23 December 2024}} Prior was signed to the practice squad of the [[New York Jets]] on September 9, 1992. He was released on September 29, 1992. He re-signed with the Jets in 1993. He played in all 16 games for the Jets during the 1993 season, recording four tackles, nine kick returns for 126 yards, and one fumble recovery. Prior appeared in 13 games in 1994, totaling four solo tackles, one assisted tackle, and 16 kick returns for 316 yards. He played in 11 games in 1995, posting one solo tackle.{{cite web | url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/P/PrioAn20.htm | title=Anthony Prior | publisher=Pro Football Reference | accessdate=23 December 2024}} He was released by the Jets on March 1, 1996. Prior was signed by the [[Cincinnati Bengals]] on March 14, 1996. He was released on July 15, 1996. He signed with the [[San Francisco 49ers]] on July 19, 1996, but was released on August 20, 1996. Prior was signed by the [[Minnesota Vikings]] on December 4, 1996, and played in three games for the team during the 1996 season. He also appeared in one playoff game that year. He became a free agent after the season and re-signed with the Vikings on April 9, 1997. Prior played in 12 games during the 1997 season before being placed on injured reserve on November 29, 1997. He was released on February 2, 1998. Prior signed with the [[Kansas City Chiefs]] on April 6, 1998. He was released on August 25, 1998. Prior was signed by the [[Oakland Raiders]] on November 4, 1998. He played in four games for the Raiders in 1998 before being released on December 2, 1998. Prior started all 18 games for the [[Calgary Stampeders]] of the [[Canadian Football League]] (CFL) in 2000, recording 75 defensive tackles, one special teams tackle, four interceptions, 14 pass breakups, and four kickoff returns for 91 yards. The Stampeders finished the year with a 12–5–1 and lost in the West Final to the [[BC Lions]].{{cite web | url=https://www.profootballarchives.com/2000cflcal.html | title=2000 Calgary Stampeders (CFL) | publisher=Pro Football Archives | accessdate=23 December 2024}} He started all 18 games for the second straight season in 2001, totaling 40 defensive tackles, two special teams tackles, one interception, 14 pass breakups, and one forced fumble. The Stampeders finished the season with an 8–10 record.{{Cite web |title=2001 Calgary Stampeders (CFL) |url=https://www.profootballarchives.com/2001cflcal.html |access-date=23 December 2024 |publisher=Pro Football Archives}} However, they ended up advancing to the [[89th Grey Cup]] on November 25, 2001, where they defeated the [[Winnipeg Blue Bombers]]. Prior played in 13 games for the [[BC Lions]] of the CFL in 2002, accumulating 32 defensive tackles, six special teams tackles, one interception, and four pass breakups. He returned to the Stampeders in 2003 and appeared in ten games for them that season, recording 25 defensive tackles and three pass breakups. ==Personal life== In 2003, Prior released a book titled ''Faith on 40 Yards: Behind the Silver & Gold of the NFL''. {{cite web | url=https://www.thenation.com/article/archive/slave-side-sunday/ | title=The Slave Side of Sunday | publisher=thenation.com | date=January 20, 2006 | accessdate=23 December 2024 | author=Zirin, Dave}} In 2006, he released another book on the NFL called ''The Slave Side of Sunday''.{{cite web | url=https://www.npr.org/2006/02/03/5187186/football-and-the-slave-side-of-sunday | title=Football and 'The Slave Side of Sunday' | publisher=Npr.org | date=February 3, 2006 | accessdate=23 December 2024}} ==References== {{reflist}} ==External links== *[https://www.justsportsstats.com/footballstatsindex.php?player_id=priorant001 Stats Crew profile] '''Anthony Morris''' (born March 25, 1992) is an American former professional [[Gridiron football|football]] player who was an [[offensive tackle]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Tennessee State Tigers football|Tennessee State Tigers]]. He was selected in the seventh round (218th overall) of the [[2015 NFL draft]] by the [[Oakland Raiders]].

==College career==
As a freshman at [[Tennessee State University]], Morris played in eight games. As a sophomore, he played in five games. He was named a full-time starter as a junior in 2013, when he played in 11 games. As a senior, he appeared in 11 games, with 10 starts.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.cbssports.com/nfl/draft/players/1852982/anthony-morris |title=Anthony Morris, OT, Tennessee State, NFL Draft |work=CBSSports.com |access-date=April 24, 2016}}</ref>

==Professional career==
Morris was selected by the [[Oakland Raiders]] in the seventh round (218th overall) of the [[2015 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=2015 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2015/draft.htm |access-date=May 15, 2023 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> He signed his rookie contract on May 12, 2015.<ref name="Transactions">{{cite web |url=http://www.foxsports.com/nfl/anthony-morris-player-transactions |title=Anthony Morris Transactions: Signings, Trades & More |work=FoxSports.com |access-date=April 24, 2016}}</ref> He was released during final cuts on September 5, 2015, with an injury designation.<ref>{{Cite web |date=September 5, 2015 |title=Raiders Cut Ponder Among Others; Finalize Regular Season Roster |url=http://losangeles.cbslocal.com/2015/09/05/raiders-cut-ponder-among-others-finalize-regular-season-roster/ |access-date=April 24, 2016 |website=CBS - Los Angeles|agency=Associated Press}}</ref><ref name="Transactions" /> On September 6, he was placed on [[injured reserve]].<ref name="Transactions" /> He was taken off of injured reserve on September 28 when he was released.<ref name="Transactions" />

Morris signed with the [[Toronto Argonauts]] of the [[Canadian Football League]] on March 2, 2017.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.argonauts.ca/2017/03/02/argos-sign-hunter-morris/ | title=Signing: Argos Add RB Hunter, OT Morris | publisher=argonauts.ca | date=March 2, 2017 | accessdate=March 17, 2017}}</ref>

He signed with the [[Memphis Express]] of the [[Alliance of American Football]] in 2018 for the 2019 season.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Nichols |first1=Meagan |date=August 17, 2018 |title=Memphis' pro football roster taking shape |url=https://www.bizjournals.com/memphis/news/2018/08/17/memphis-pro-football-roster-taking-shape.html |accessdate=November 29, 2018 |website=bizjournals.com}}</ref> He was placed on injured reserve on March 7, 2019, and activated from injured reserve on April 1. The league ceased operations in April 2019.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Rothstein |first=Michael |last2=Wickersham |first2=Seth |date=June 13, 2019 |title=Inside the short, unhappy life of the Alliance of American Football |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/26957796/inside-short-unhappy-life-alliance-american-football |access-date=January 9, 2024 |website=[[ESPN.com]]}}</ref>

Morris was selected by the [[Los Angeles Wildcats (XFL)|Los Angeles Wildcats]] of the [[XFL (2020)|XFL]] in the 10th round in phase 2 of the [[2020 XFL draft]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.xfl.com/en-US/articles/phase-2-offensive-line-draft-tracker |title=OFFENSIVE LINEMEN DRAFT TRACKER |website=XFL.com |date=October 15, 2019 |accessdate=October 16, 2019}}</ref> He was placed on [[injured reserve]] on December 17, 2019.<ref>{{cite news |title=WILDCATS ANNOUNCE MINICAMP TRANSACTIONS |url=https://www.xfl.com/articles/los-angeles-wildcats-announce-minicamp-transactions |website=XFL.com |date=December 17, 2019 |accessdate=December 19, 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=XFL Injured Reserve |url=https://www.xfl.com/en-US/xfl-injured-reserve |website=XFL.com |accessdate=February 6, 2020}}</ref> He had his contract terminated when the league suspended operations on April 10, 2020.<ref>{{cite news |author=Condotta, Bob |title=XFL suspends operations, terminates all employees, but Jim Zorn says he has hopes league will continue |url=https://www.seattletimes.com/sports/xfl-suspends-operations-terminates-all-employees/ |website=SeattleTimes.com |date=April 10, 2020 |accessdate=July 17, 2020}}</ref>

Morris signed with the Conquerors of [[The Spring League]] in May 2021.<ref>{{cite tweet |user=TheSpringLeague |title=First look at the #TSLConquerors roster at #TSL2021! |number=1389389947283640322 |date=May 3, 2021 |access-date=June 22, 2021}}</ref>

'''Anthony Lanier II''' (born May 8, 1993) is an American professional [[gridiron football|football]] [[defensive end]]. He most recently played for the [[Toronto Argonauts]] of the [[Canadian Football League]] (CFL). He played [[college football]] at [[Alabama A&M]] and was signed by the [[Washington Redskins]] as an [[undrafted free agent]] in 2016.

==Professional career==
[[File:Anthony Lanier 2016.jpg|thumb|left|200px|Lanier with the Washington Redskins in 2016]]
===Washington Redskins===
After going unselected in the [[2016 NFL draft]], Lanier signed with the [[Washington Redskins]] on May 6, 2016.<ref>{{cite news|work=WashingtonPost.com|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/news/football-insider/wp/2016/05/06/redskins-sign-seven-more-undrafted-free-agents/|title=Redskins sign seven more undrafted free agents|first=Mike |last=Jones |date=May 6, 2016|access-date=September 3, 2016}}</ref> Standing out in training camp and the preseason, the team announced he made the 53-man roster on September 3.<ref>{{cite news|work=WashingtonPost.com|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/news/football-insider/wp/2016/08/21/redskins-defense-snap-counts-vs-the-jets-rookie-anthony-lanier-shines-on-the-defensive-line/|title=Redskins' defense snap counts vs. the Jets: Rookie Anthony Lanier shines|first=Master |last=Tesfatsion |date=August 2, 2016|access-date=September 3, 2016}}</ref> In his NFL debut in Week 8, Lanier recovered a fumble forced by [[Chris Baker (defensive lineman)|Chris Baker]] on [[2016 Cincinnati Bengals season|Cincinnati Bengals]] quarterback [[Andy Dalton]]. He was placed on injured reserve on December 13.<ref>{{cite web|title=Redskins Sign Linebacker Nick Moody, Place Anthony Lanier On Injured Reserve|url=http://www.redskins.com/news/article-1/Redskins-Sign-Linebacker-Nick-Moody-Place-Anthony-Lanier-On-Injured-Reserve/e2455046-3fba-4281-88f4-14f837a53fd1|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170903032927/http://www.redskins.com/news/article-1/Redskins-Sign-Linebacker-Nick-Moody-Place-Anthony-Lanier-On-Injured-Reserve/e2455046-3fba-4281-88f4-14f837a53fd1|url-status=dead|archive-date=September 3, 2017|author=Czarda, Stephen|website=Redskins.com|date=December 13, 2016}}</ref>

Lanier was inactive for the first six games of [[2017 Washington Redskins season|2017]]. In Week 11 against the [[2017 New Orleans Saints season|New Orleans Saints]], he recorded first career sack on [[Drew Brees]].<ref>{{cite web|work=Redskins.com|url=http://www.redskins.com/news/article-1/Redskins-Saints-Monday-Stats-Pack/fcef7dd3-49ce-4073-91c1-bb810b8d869c|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171225092205/http://www.redskins.com/news/article-1/Redskins-Saints-Monday-Stats-Pack/fcef7dd3-49ce-4073-91c1-bb810b8d869c|url-status=dead|archive-date=December 25, 2017|title=Redskins-Saints Monday Stats Pack|date=November 20, 2017|access-date=December 24, 2017}}</ref> He would have a breakout performance in Week 15 against the [[2017 Arizona Cardinals season|Arizona Cardinals]] recording two sacks, three pass deflections, and a forced fumble.<ref>{{cite news|work=WashingtonPost.com|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/the-sky-is-the-limit-for-him-anthony-lanier-delivers-breakout-game-for-redskins/2017/12/17/616da3e6-e370-11e7-a65d-1ac0fd7f097e_story.html|title='The sky is the limit for him': Anthony Lanier delivers breakout game for Redskins|first=Kimberley|last=Martin|date=December 17, 2017|access-date=August 11, 2018}}</ref> On September 3, 2018, the Redskins waived/injured Lanier.<ref>{{cite web|work=Redskins.com|url=https://www.redskins.com/news/redskins-sign-caleb-brantley-waive-anthony-lanier-ii|date=September 3, 2018|title=Redskins Sign Caleb Brantley, Waive Anthony Lanier II|first=Jake |last=Kring-Schreifels|access-date=September 3, 2018}}</ref> He went unclaimed in the waiver stage, and reverted to the team's injured reserve list before being waived with an injury settlement on September 8.<ref>{{cite web |title=9/8: Redskins Make Roster Move |url=https://www.redskins.com/news/9-8-redskins-make-roster-move |website=Redskins.com |access-date=September 8, 2018}}</ref>

===Los Angeles Chargers===
On November 7, 2018, Lanier was signed to the [[Los Angeles Chargers]]' practice squad.<ref>{{cite web|title=Chargers Sign Anthony Lanier, Kyle Wilson to Practice Squad|url=https://www.chargers.com/news/chargers-sign-anthony-lanier-kyle-wilson-to-practice-squad|author=Henne, Ricky|website=Chargers.com|date=November 7, 2018}}</ref> He was promoted to the active roster on December 20.<ref>{{cite web|title=Chargers Promote Anthony Lanier, Waive Chris Landrum|url=https://www.chargers.com/news/chargers-promote-anthony-lanier-waive-chris-landrum|author=Henne, Ricky|website=Chargers.com|date=December 20, 2018}}</ref>

On August 31, 2019, Lanier was waived by the Chargers; he was re-signed to the team's practice squad the next day.<ref>{{cite web|title=Chargers Announce Roster Moves|url=https://www.chargers.com/news/chargers-announce-roster-moves-x6572|website=Chargers.com|date=August 31, 2019|access-date=September 7, 2019|archive-date=August 11, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200811132710/https://www.chargers.com/news/chargers-announce-roster-moves-x6572|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Chargers Announce Practice Squad|url=https://www.chargers.com/news/chargers-announce-practice-squad|website=Chargers.com|date=September 1, 2019|access-date=September 7, 2019|archive-date=September 20, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190920080438/https://www.chargers.com/news/chargers-announce-practice-squad|url-status=dead}}</ref> His practice squad contract with the team expired on January 6, 2020.<ref>{{cite tweet |user=HBalzer721 |title=Chargers practice-squad contracts expired Monday: WR Anthony Johnson; DE Anthony Lanier; WR Artavis Scott. |number=1214637619361075201 |date=January 7, 2020 |accessdate=January 9, 2020}}</ref>

===Kansas City Chiefs===
On January 8, 2020, Lanier signed a reserve/future contract with the [[Kansas City Chiefs]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Chiefs sign DE Anthony Lanier to reserve/future contract|url=https://chiefswire.usatoday.com/2020/01/08/kansas-city-chiefs-sign-de-anthony-lanier-to-reserve-future-contract/|work=Chiefs Wire|publisher=USA Today|date=January 8, 2020}}</ref> He was waived by the Chiefs on April 28.<ref>{{cite news |author=Goldman, Charles |title=Chiefs release DE Anthony Lanier |url=https://chiefswire.usatoday.com/2020/04/29/kansas-city-chiefs-release-de-anthony-lanier/ |website=USAToday.com |date=April 28, 2020 |access-date=May 1, 2020}}</ref>

Lanier had a tryout with the [[Detroit Lions]] on August 19, 2020.<ref>{{cite tweet |user=AlbertBreer |title=Today’s workouts/visits. |number=1296191904980312070 |date=August 19, 2020 |accessdate=August 21, 2020}}</ref>

=== New Orleans Saints ===
Lanier was signed by the [[New Orleans Saints]] on August 29, 2020.<ref>{{Cite web|date=August 29, 2020|title=Saints fill out the roster with former Chiefs, Chargers pass rusher Anthony Lanier|url=https://saintswire.usatoday.com/2020/08/29/saints-roster-chiefs-chargers-anthony-lanier/|access-date=August 29, 2020|website=Saints Wire|language=en-US}}</ref> He was placed on injured reserve on September 5,<ref>{{cite web|title=Saints announce 53-man roster reductions for 2020|url=https://www.neworleanssaints.com/news/new-orleans-saints-roster-2020-nfl-roster-cuts-53-man|website=NewOrleansSaints.com|date=September 5, 2020}}</ref> and waived with an injury settlement on September 11.<ref>{{cite news |title=Anthony Lanier: Waived with injury settlement |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/football/news/anthony-lanier-waived-with-injury-settlement/ |website=CBSSports.com |date=September 11, 2020 |access-date=September 16, 2020}}</ref>

===Saskatchewan Roughriders===
Lanier signed with the [[Saskatchewan Roughriders]] of the CFL on March 2, 2021.<ref>{{cite news |title=Riders sign American defensive lineman Anthony Lanier II |url=https://www.riderville.com/2021/03/02/riders-sign-american-defensive-lineman-anthony-lanier-ii/ |website=Riderville.com |date=March 2, 2021 |access-date=March 2, 2021}}</ref>

=== Toronto Argonauts ===
On February 12, 2025, it was announced that Lanier had signed a contract with the [[Toronto Argonauts]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-02-12 |title=Argos sign four, including Anthony Lanier II and Ciante Evans |url=https://www.cfl.ca/2025/02/12/argos-sign-four-including-anthony-lanier-ii-and-ciante-evans/ |access-date=2025-02-12 |website=CFL.ca |language=en}}</ref> He spent one year with Toronto and became a free agent upon the expiry of his contract on February 10, 2026.<ref name=2026T>{{Cite web |url=https://www.cfl.ca/transactions/2026/ |title=Transactions – Football player trades and signings |publisher=[[Canadian Football League]] |access-date=February 13, 2026}}</ref>

'''Anthony Laron Walker Jr.''' (born August 8, 1995) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[linebacker]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Northwestern Wildcats football|Northwestern Wildcats]] and was selected by the [[Indianapolis Colts]] in the fifth round of the [[2017 NFL draft]].

==College career==
Walker first saw action in his [[redshirted|redshirt]] freshman season when Collin Ellis went down with a series of injuries. In his first career game, Walker returned an [[interception]] for a [[touchdown]] against [[Penn State Nittany Lions football|Penn State]] that capped a Northwestern win. In his first full season as a starter, Walker found success as he recorded 122 [[tackled gridiron|tackles]] to lead the team and 20.5 tackles for loss which was fourth in the nation. For his performance that season, Walker received [[College Football All-America Team|All-American]] recognition from the [[Associated Press]] and ''[[Sports Illustrated]]'' as well as Consensus First-team [[List of All-Big Ten Conference football teams|All-Big Ten Conference]] honors.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Anthony Walker Jr. Bio |url=http://www.nusports.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=4723 |publisher=NorthWestern University Football - Official Website}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Anthony Walker, Northwestern, Inside Linebacker |url=https://247sports.com/Player/Anthony-Walker-10371 |access-date=October 3, 2016 |publisher=247 Sports}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Anthony Walker College Stats |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/anthony-walker-1.html |access-date=October 3, 2016 |publisher=College Football at Sorts-Reference.com}}</ref> On November 29, 2016, Walker was named Second-team All-Big Ten.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2016 Big Ten Individual Award Winners |url=http://grfx.cstv.com/photos/schools/big10/sports/m-footbl/auto_pdf/2016-17/misc_non_event/FBTuesAllB1G.pdf |access-date=November 30, 2016 |website=www.grfx.cstv.com |publisher=Big Ten Conference |archive-date=November 29, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161129231830/http://grfx.cstv.com/photos/schools/big10/sports/m-footbl/auto_pdf/2016-17/misc_non_event/FBTuesAllB1G.pdf |url-status=dead }}</ref>

===Indianapolis Colts===
====2017====
The [[Indianapolis Colts]] selected Walker in the fifth round (161st overall) of the [[2017 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=2017 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2017/draft.htm |access-date=2023-05-17 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> Walker was the 20th [[linebacker]] drafted in 2017.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bowen, Kevin |date=April 29, 2017 |title=Colts Draft Northwestern Linebacker Anthony Walker, Jr. In Round Five |url=http://www.colts.com/news/article-draft/Colts-Draft-Northwestern-Linebacker-Anthony-Walker-Jr-In-Round-Five/65c78bd2-2e4b-4c13-a479-6c632d478b7c |access-date=May 9, 2017 |website=Colts.com}}</ref>
{{external media
| video1 =
[http://www.nfl.com/videos/nfl-draft/0ap3000000804767/Colts-select-Anthony-Walker-Jr-No-161-in-the-2017-NFL-Draft Colts draft Anthony Walker 161st overall]
}}
On May 11, 2017, the Colts signed Walker to a four-year, $2.66 million contract that includes a [[signing bonus]] of $265,413.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Spotrac.com: Anthony Walker Jr. contract |url=https://www.spotrac.com/nfl/indianapolis-colts/anthony-walker-jr-21903/ |access-date=October 1, 2018 |website=Spotrac.com}}</ref>

Walker missed [[organized team activities]] due to Northwestern's quarters schedule and the league's rules on rookies being unable to join their team until their school's final semester had concluded.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Hickey, Kevin |date=July 17, 2017 |title=Bleacher Report: Sean Spence, Anthony Walker should start at ILB |url=https://coltswire.usatoday.com/2017/07/17/indianapolis-colts-sean-spence-anthony-walker-start-inside-linebacker/ |access-date=October 1, 2018 |website=coltswire.usatoday.com}}</ref> Upon entering [[training camp (NFL)|training camp]], Walker competed to be a starting inside linebacker against [[Sean Spence]], [[Antonio Morrison (American football)|Antonio Morrison]], [[Jon Bostic]], and [[Edwin Jackson (American football)|Edwin Jackson]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=July 27, 2017 |title=Analyzing the Indianapolis Colts' Inside Linebacker Position Battle |url=http://www.indianasportscoverage.com/analyzing-the-indianapolis-colts-inside-linebacker-position-battle/ |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181002021542/http://www.indianasportscoverage.com/analyzing-the-indianapolis-colts-inside-linebacker-position-battle/ |archive-date=October 2, 2018 |access-date=October 1, 2018 |website=indianasportscoverage.com}}</ref> Head coach [[Chuck Pagano]] named Walker a backup inside linebacker to begin the regular season, behind Bostic and Morrison.<ref>{{Cite web |date=September 5, 2018 |title=First Look at the 2017 Colts Regular Season Depth Chart |url=https://www.stampedeblue.com/2017/9/5/16257616/first-look-at-the-2017-colts-regular-season-depth-chart |access-date=October 1, 2018 |website=stampedeblue.com}}</ref>

He made his professional regular season debut in the Colts' season-opener at the [[Los Angeles Rams]], but exited in the second quarter of their 46–9 loss after sustaining a [[hamstring]] injury.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Hickey, Kevin |date=September 10, 2017 |title=Colts' Anthony Walker (hamstring) out vs. Rams |url=https://coltswire.usatoday.com/2017/09/10/indianapolis-colts-anthony-walker-hamstring-out-los-angeles-rams/ |access-date=October 1, 2018 |website=coltswire.usatoday.com}}</ref> His hamstring injury sidelined him for the next three games (Weeks 2–4). In Week 5, he aggravated his hamstring injury during the third quarter of a 26–23 win against the [[San Francisco 49ers]] and was inactive for the next three games (Weeks 6–8).<ref>{{Cite web |title=Colts' Anthony Walker Jr.: Leaves game with hamstring injury |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/football/news/colts-anthony-walker-jr-leaves-game-with-hamstring-injury/ |access-date=October 1, 2018 |website=cbssports.com}}</ref> On December 29, 2017, Walker earned his first start after Jon Bostic was ruled inactive due to an injury. He collected a season-high nine combined tackles in the Colts' 23–16 loss at the [[Baltimore Ravens]] in Week 16.<ref>{{Cite web |title=NFL Player stats: Anthony Walker Jr. (2017) |url=http://www.nfl.com/player/anthonywalker/2558851/gamelogs?season=2017 |access-date=October 1, 2018 |website=NFL.com}}</ref> On December 31, the  Colts fired Pagano after they finished the season with a 4–12 record.<ref>{{Cite web |date=December 31, 2017 |title=Indianapolis Colts fire Chuck Pagano after 4-12 year |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/indianapolis-colts-fire-chuck-pagano-after-4-12-year-0ap3000000900837 |access-date=October 1, 2018 |website=NFL.com}}</ref> He finished his rookie season in 2017 with 22 combined tackles (11 solo) in ten games and two starts.<ref name="career">{{Cite web |title=NFL Player stats: Anthony Walker Jr. (career) |url=http://www.nfl.com/player/anthonywalker/2558851/careerstats |access-date=October 1, 2018 |website=NFL.com}}</ref>

====2018====
On February 11, 2018, the Colts hired former [[Philadelphia Eagles]] offensive coordinator [[Frank Reich]] as their new head coach.<ref>{{Cite web |date=February 11, 2018 |title=Indianapolis Colts hire Frank Reich to be next coach |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/indianapolis-colts-hire-frank-reich-to-be-next-coach-0ap3000000915859 |access-date=October 1, 2018 |website=NFL.com}}</ref> Defensive coordinator [[Matt Eberflus]] opted to change the base [[3-4 defense]] and implemented a base [[4-3 defense]]. Walker entered training camp slated as the starting middle linebacker, but saw competition from [[Najee Goode]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Predicting Who Will Start at Linebacker for the Indianapolis Colts |url=http://www.indianasportscoverage.com/predicting-who-will-start-at-linebacker-for-the-indianapolis-colts/ |access-date=October 1, 2018 |website=indianasportscoverage.com |archive-date=January 31, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200131001813/http://indianasportscoverage.com/predicting-who-will-start-at-linebacker-for-the-indianapolis-colts/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> On July 31, it was reported that Walker had injured his groin in the first week of training camp and was sidelined for the remainder of training camp and all four preseason games.<ref>{{Cite web |date=September 3, 2018 |title=After Missing Most Of Training Camp, Anthony Walker 'Full-Go' For Week 1 |url=https://www.colts.com/news/after-missing-most-of-training-camp-anthony-walker-full-go-for-week-1 |access-date=October 1, 2018 |website=Colts.com}}</ref> Head coach Frank Reich named Walker the starting middle linebacker to start the regular season in 2018, alongside outside linebackers Najee Goode and rookie [[Shaquille Leonard]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Andrew Walker |date=September 4, 2018 |title=Colts Release First Unofficial Depth Chart Of 2018 Regular Season |url=https://www.colts.com/news/colts-release-first-unofficial-depth-chart-of-2018-regular-season |access-date=October 1, 2018 |website=Colts.com}}</ref>

On September 23, Walker recorded nine combined tackles and made his first career interception off a pass by quarterback [[Carson Wentz]] during a 20–16 loss at the Eagles in Week 2.<ref>{{Cite web |title=NFL Player stats: Anthony Walker Jr. (2018) |url=http://www.nfl.com/player/anthonywalker/2558851/gamelogs?season=2018 |access-date=October 1, 2018 |website=NFL.com}}</ref>

====2019====
In Week 13 against the [[Tennessee Titans]], Walker recorded a team-high 12 tackles and forced a [[fumble]] on running back [[Derrick Henry]] on the first play of the game which was recovered by teammate [[Malik Hooker]] in the 31–17 loss.<ref>{{Cite web |date=December 1, 2019 |title=Blocked field goal helps Titans turn table with win at Indy |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/recap?gameId=401128058 |access-date=December 1, 2019 |website=[[ESPN]]}}</ref>
In Week 16 against the [[Carolina Panthers]], Walker recorded 10 tackles, sacked rookie quarterback [[Will Grier]] once, and intercepted a pass thrown by Grier during the 38–6 win.<ref>{{Cite web |date=December 22, 2019 |title=Hines' long returns help send Colts past Carolina 38-6 |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/recap?gameId=401127906 |access-date=December 22, 2019 |website=[[ESPN]] |agency=Associated Press}}</ref>
In Week 17 against the [[Jacksonville Jaguars]], Walker recorded a team high 16 tackles during the 38–20 loss.<ref>{{Cite web |date=December 29, 2019 |title=Minshew, Jaguars close out season with 38-20 win over Colts |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/recap?gameId=401127988 |access-date=December 29, 2019 |website=[[ESPN]] |agency=Associated Press}}</ref>

====2020====
In Week 5 against the [[2020 Cleveland Browns season|Cleveland Browns]], Walker recorded his first interception off a pass thrown by [[Baker Mayfield]] during the 32–23 loss.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Indianapolis Colts at Cleveland Browns - October 11th, 2020 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202010110cle.htm |access-date=October 11, 2020 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> In Week 13 against the [[2020 Houston Texans season|Houston Texans]], Walker recovered a fumble lost by [[Deshaun Watson]] late in the fourth quarter to secure a 26–20 win for the Colts.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Indianapolis Colts at Houston Texans - December 6th, 2020 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202012060htx.htm |access-date=December 8, 2020 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

===Cleveland Browns===
====2021====
On March 19, 2021, Walker signed a one-year contract with the [[Cleveland Browns]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Gribble, Andrew |date=March 19, 2021 |title=Browns sign Anthony Walker, a 'smart, tough' linebacker |url=https://www.clevelandbrowns.com/news/browns-sign-anthony-walker-a-smart-tough-linebacker |website=ClevelandBrowns.com}}</ref> Walker was placed on injured reserve with a hamstring injury on September 17.<ref>{{cite news |title=Browns place LB Anthony Walker on injured reserve |url=https://www.clevelandbrowns.com/news/browns-place-lb-anthony-walker-on-injured-reserve |publisher=ClevelandBrowns.com |date=September 17, 2021}}</ref> He was activated on October 9 for Week 5.<ref>{{cite web|title=Browns make roster moves|url=https://www.clevelandbrowns.com/news/browns-make-roster-moves-x7845|website=ClevelandBrowns.com|date=October 9, 2021}}</ref>

====2022====
On March 16, 2022, Walker re-signed with the Browns on a one-year contract.<ref>{{cite web|title=Browns agree to terms with LB Anthony Walker Jr., OL Chris Hubbard|url=https://www.clevelandbrowns.com/news/browns-agree-to-terms-with-lb-anthony-walker-jr-ol-chris-hubbard|website=ClevelandBrowns.com|date=March 16, 2022}}</ref> He suffered a [[quadriceps tendon rupture|torn quad]] in Week 3 and was placed on injured reserve on September 23.<ref>{{cite web|title=Browns place LB Anthony Walker Jr. on injured reserve|url=https://www.clevelandbrowns.com/news/browns-place-lb-anthony-walker-jr-on-injured-reserve|website=ClevelandBrowns.com|date=September 23, 2022}}</ref>

====2023====
On March 29, 2023, Walker re-signed with the Browns on another one-year contract.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.clevelandbrowns.com/news/browns-re-sign-lb-anthony-walker-jr|work=ClevelandBrowns.com|title=Browns re-sign LB Anthony Walker Jr.|date=March 29, 2023|accessdate=March 30, 2023|first=Anthony|last=Poisal}}</ref> He was placed on injured reserve on January 5, 2024.<ref>{{cite web |title=Browns place LB Anthony Walker Jr. on injured reserve |url=https://www.clevelandbrowns.com/news/browns-place-lb-anthony-walker-jr-on-injured-reserve-x0371 |website=clevelandbrowns.com |access-date=5 January 2024}}</ref> He started 12 games in 2023, recording 44 tackles, four passes defended, and a forced fumble.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Anthony Walker 2023 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/W/WalkAn01/gamelog/2023/ |access-date=2024-12-27 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

===Miami Dolphins ===
On March 15, 2024, Walker signed with the [[Miami Dolphins]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Miami Dolphins Sign Anthony Walker Jr. |url=https://www.miamidolphins.com/news/miami-dolphins-sign-anthony-walker-jr|date=March 15, 2024|website=MiamiDolphins.com |language=en-US}}</ref> He played in 14 games with eight starts, recording 68 tackles, one sack, two passes defended, and one interception.

===Tampa Bay Buccaneers===
On March 19, 2025, Walker signed a one-year contract with the [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Bucs Bolster LB Crew with Former Dolphin Anthony Walker|url=https://www.buccaneers.com/news/bucs-bolster-lb-crew-former-dolphin-anthony-walker|author=Smith, Scott|website=Buccaneers.com|date=March 19, 2025}}</ref> On August 25, Walker was released by the Buccaneers with a non-football injury designation.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Anthony Walker: Released by Tampa Bay|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/football/news/anthony-walker-released-by-tampa-bay/|access-date=October 27, 2025|website=cbssports.com|language=en}}</ref>

===Indianapolis Colts (second stint)===
On September 1, 2025, Walker was signed to the [[Indianapolis Colts]]' practice squad.<ref>{{cite web |title=Colts bring back former starting linebacker Anthony Walker Jr. by adding him to the practice squad |website=[[WTHR]] |url=https://www.wthr.com/article/sports/local-sports/colts-bring-back-former-starting-linebacker-anthony-walker-jr-by-adding-him-to-the-practice-squad-josh-tupou-indianapolis-indiana/531-3513257e-1f48-44a8-a13c-957b1a79298f |date=September 1, 2025 |access-date=September 1, 2025}}</ref>

===Tampa Bay Buccaneers (second stint)===
On December 15, 2025, Walker was signed by the Tampa Bay Buccaneers off of the Colts' practice squad.<ref>{{cite web|title=Bucs Put Zyon McCollum on Injured Reserve Among Flurry of Week 16 Moves|url=https://www.buccaneers.com/news/bucs-zyon-mccollum-injured-reserve-among-flurry-week-16-moves|author=Smith, Scott|website=Buccaneers.com|date=December 15, 2025}}</ref>

Walker announced his retirement from professional football on April 2, 2026, after nine seasons in the NFL.<ref>{{Cite web|title=LB Anthony Walker retires from NFL after nine seasons|url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/48378935/lb-anthony-walker-retires-nfl-nine-seasons|work=ESPN|date=April 2, 2026|access-date=April 3, 2026}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Walker wore the number 4 for the Browns until [[Deshaun Watson trade|Deshaun Watson was traded]] to the team in 2022. Watson gave Walker a new [[Rolex]] watch in exchange for the number, despite Walker not requesting anything. Following the swap, Walker wore number 5.<ref name="y274">{{cite web | last=Rapp | first=Timothy | title=Deshaun Watson Gifts Anthony Walker a Rolex for No. 4 Browns Jersey | website=Bleacher Report | date=2022-05-25 | url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/10036902-deshaun-watson-gifts-anthony-walker-a-rolex-for-no-4-browns-jersey | access-date=2024-10-01}}</ref>

'''Anthony Kukwa''' (born October 30, 1992) is an American former [[American football|football]] [[long snapper]]. He initially attended [[Ball State Cardinals football|Ball State University]] and later transferred to [[Lake Erie College]], where he played long snapper and [[tight end]]. Kukwa is Lake Erie's first ever student-athlete to sign an NFL contract.

==Professional career==
===Oakland Raiders===
Kukwa signed with the [[Oakland Raiders]] as an undrafted free agent on May 5, 2017.<ref>{{cite web|title=Raiders Announce Undrafted Free Agent Signings|url=http://www.raiders.com/news/article-1/Raiders-Announce-Undrafted-Free-Agent-Signings/5a719ac0-ebd7-40c8-bbfe-9266c5d3c3c2|website=Raiders.com|date=May 5, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170929165652/http://www.raiders.com/news/article-1/Raiders-Announce-Undrafted-Free-Agent-Signings/5a719ac0-ebd7-40c8-bbfe-9266c5d3c3c2|access-date=June 24, 2017|archive-date=September 29, 2017}}</ref> He was waived by the Raiders on July 7, 2017.<ref>{{cite web|title=Raiders Announce Transactions|url=http://www.raiders.com/news/article-1/Raiders-Announce-Transactions/55397347-d8df-49c3-8abc-b55dc19919fa?sf96293637=1|website=Raiders.com|date=July 7, 2017|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20180105070712/http://www.raiders.com/news/article-1/Raiders-Announce-Transactions/55397347-d8df-49c3-8abc-b55dc19919fa?sf96293637=1|archive-date = January 5, 2018}}</ref>

===Los Angeles Chargers===
On January 4, 2018, Kukwa signed a reserve/future contract with the [[Los Angeles Chargers]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Perry grad Anthony Kukwa signs NFL futures contract with Chargers|url=http://www.news-herald.com/sports/20180107/perry-grad-anthony-kukwa-signs-nfl-futures-contract-with-chargers|website=News-Herald.com|date=January 7, 2018|access-date=March 24, 2018}}</ref> On May 30, 2018, he was waived by the Chargers.<ref>{{cite web|title=Bolts Sign TE Austin Roberts|url=http://www.chargers.com/news/2018/05/30/bolts-sign-te-austin-roberts|author=Henne, Ricky|website=Chargers.com|date=May 30, 2018}}</ref>

===Houston Texans===
Kukwa had a mini-camp tryout with the [[Houston Texans]] in 2019, but was not signed to a contract. He signed with the team on April 25, 2020.<ref>{{cite news |author=Wilson, Aaron |title=Texans sign long snapper Anthony Kukwa |url=https://www.chron.com/sports/texans/article/Texans-sign-long-snapper-Anthony-Kukwa-15227825.php |website=Chron.com |date=April 26, 2020 |access-date=April 28, 2020}}</ref> He was waived on July 27, 2020.<ref>{{cite news |title=Texans Announce Roster Moves |url=https://www.houstontexans.com/news/texans-make-roster-moves |website=HoustonTexans.com |date=July 27, 2020 |access-date=July 28, 2020}}</ref> Kukwa had a tryout with the Texans on August 20, 2020,<ref>{{cite tweet |user=AlbertBreer |title=Today's tryout/visit list. |number=1296557572107968514 |date=August 20, 2020 |accessdate=August 21, 2020}}</ref> and re-signed with the team three days later.<ref>{{cite news |title=Texans Announce Roster Moves |url=https://www.houstontexans.com/news/texans-announce-roster-moves-x8876 |website=HoustonTexans.com |date=August 23, 2020 |access-date=August 24, 2020}}</ref> He was waived on September 5, 2020.<ref>{{Cite web |date=September 5, 2020 |title=Transactions: Roster Moves (9-5-2020) |url=https://www.houstontexans.com/news/transactions-roster-moves-9-5-2020 |access-date=2025-08-16 |website=HoustonTexans.com}}</ref> On December 15, 2020, Kukwa made his first official NFL regular season roster, by being signed to the [[2020 Houston Texans season|2020 Houston Texans]] Practice Squad.
<ref>{{Cite news |date=December 15, 2020 |title=Houston Texans Transactions (12-15-20) |url=https://www.houstontexans.com/news/houston-texans-transactions-12-15-20 |access-date=2025-08-16 |work=HoustonTexans.com}}</ref> He signed a reserve/future contract on January 4, 2021.<ref>{{Cite web |date=January 4, 2021 |title=Houston Texans Transactions (1-4-21) |url=https://www.houstontexans.com/news/houston-texans-transactions-1-4-21 |access-date=2025-08-16 |website=HoustonTexans.com}}</ref> He was waived on March 23, 2021.<ref>{{Cite web |date=March 23, 2021 |title=Houston Texans Transactions (3-23-2021) |url=https://www.houstontexans.com/news/houston-texans-transactions-3-23-2021 |access-date=March 23, 2021 |website=HoustonTexans.com}}</ref>

'''Anthony Miller''' (born October 9, 1994) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[wide receiver]]. He played [[college football]] for the [[Memphis Tigers football|Memphis Tigers]].

==Early life==
Miller attended [[Christian Brothers High School (Memphis, Tennessee)|Christian Brothers High School]] in [[Memphis, Tennessee]], where he played [[high school football|football]] and ran [[track and field|track]] for the Purple Wave athletic teams.<ref name="memphisdailynews" />

==College career==
Miller joined the [[University of Memphis]] football team as a [[Walk-on (sports)|walk-on]].<ref name="commercialappeal">{{Cite web |last=Schad |first=Tom |date=October 14, 2015 |title=U of M's Anthony Miller goes from walk-on to key WR |url=http://archive.commercialappeal.com/sports/tigers/football/u-of-ms-anthony-miller-goes-from-walk-on-to-key-wr-2212833d-6d13-2661-e053-0100007fd58a-332932931.html |access-date=November 20, 2022 |website=Commercial Appeal}}</ref> He redshirted in 2013 and then again in 2014 due to an injury. In 2015, he played in 12 games and made four starts, recording 47 [[football catch|receptions]] for 694 yards with five receiving [[touchdowns]] and two rushing touchdowns. In 2016, Miller started all 13 games and set school records with 95 receptions for 1,434 yards and 14 touchdowns.<ref name="commercialappeal2">{{Cite web |last=Schad |first=Tom |date=March 18, 2017 |title=Inside Anthony Miller's decision to return to Memphis |url=http://www.commercialappeal.com/story/sports/college/memphis-tigers/football/2017/03/18/inside-anthony-millers-decision-return-memphis/99350912/ |access-date=November 20, 2022 |website=Commercial Appeal}}</ref><ref name="memphisdailynews">{{Cite web |last=Wade |first=Don |date=November 3, 2017 |title=Anthony Miller: A Great Catch for Memphis |url=https://www.memphisdailynews.com/news/2017/nov/3/anthony-miller-a-great-catch-for-memphis/ |access-date=November 20, 2022 |website=Memphis Daily News}}</ref> During his senior season in 2017, he broke [[Duke Calhoun]]'s school records for career receptions and receiving yards, [[Carlos Singleton]]'s school record for career receiving touchdowns, and his own outright record for single-season receiving touchdowns and shared record for single-game receiving touchdowns.<ref name="usatoday">{{Cite web |last=Melo |first=Justin |date=November 13, 2017 |title=Meet Anthony Miller, the walk-on who rewrote the Memphis record books |url=http://draftwire.usatoday.com/2017/11/13/anthony-miller-memphis-antonio-brown-odell-beckham/ |access-date=November 20, 2022 |website=The Draft Wire}}</ref><ref name="commercialappeal3">{{Cite web |last=Calkins |first=Geoff |date=October 28, 2017 |title=Memphis Tigers receiver Anthony Miller is smashing records – and teaching lessons |url=http://www.commercialappeal.com/story/sports/columnists/geoff-calkins/2017/10/28/memphis-tigers-receiver-anthony-miller-smashing-records-and-teaching-lessons/809816001/ |access-date=November 20, 2022 |website=Commercial Appeal}}</ref>

===Chicago Bears===
====2018====
Miller was selected by the [[Chicago Bears]] in the second round, 51st overall, of the [[2018 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Mayer |first=Larry |date=April 27, 2018 |title=Bears trade up to select Miller in Round 2 |url=http://www.chicagobears.com/news/article-1/Bears-trade-up-to-select-Miller-in-Round-2/55ee9922-b3b4-43c5-8b6e-4d8878f799f9 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180527023447/http://www.chicagobears.com/news/article-1/Bears-trade-up-to-select-Miller-in-Round-2/55ee9922-b3b4-43c5-8b6e-4d8878f799f9 |archive-date=May 27, 2018 |access-date=September 19, 2019 |website=ChicagoBears.com}}</ref> He was the sixth wide receiver to be selected that year.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2018 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2018/draft.htm |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

In his NFL debut against the [[Green Bay Packers]] in the season opener, he had two receptions for 14 yards in the 24–23 defeat.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Kane |first=Colleen |date=September 12, 2018 |title=11 things we heard from Bears assistant coaches about Mitch Trubisky's 'happy feet,' Kyle Fuller's dropped INT and more |work=Chicago Tribune |url=http://www.chicagotribune.com/sports/football/bears/ct-spt-bears-mitch-trubisky-kyle-fuller-assistant-coaches-20180912-story.html |access-date=September 19, 2019}}</ref> In the following game, a 24–17 victory over the [[Seattle Seahawks]], he recorded his first professional touchdown reception.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Greer |first=Jarvis |date=September 18, 2018 |title=Anthony Miller scores first NFL touchdown |work=WMC Action News 5 |url=https://www.wmcactionnews5.com/2018/09/18/anthony-miller-scores-first-nfl-touchdown/ |access-date=September 19, 2019}}</ref> The third game of the year against the [[Arizona Cardinals]] saw Miller catch four passes for 35 yards, but he left the game early with a dislocated shoulder.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Wiltfong Jr. |first=Lester A. |date=September 24, 2018 |title=Bears' Anthony Miller dislocated his shoulder |url=https://www.windycitygridiron.com/2018/9/23/17893768/chicago-bears-anthony-miller-leaves-game-twice-with-an-injury-shoulder |access-date=September 19, 2019 |work=Windy City Gridiron|publisher=SB Nation}}</ref>

On October 14, caught a 29-yard touchdown pass against the [[Miami Dolphins]], his second of the season, in the 31–28 overtime loss.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Dickerson |first=Jeff |date=October 15, 2018 |title=Bears' Mitchell Trubisky keeps on uptick with sizzling second half |work=ESPN.com |url=https://www.espn.com/blog/nfcnorth/post/_/id/82265/bears-mitchell-trubisky-keeps-on-uptick-with-sizzling-second-half |access-date=September 19, 2019}}</ref> Two weeks later, Miller caught three passes for 37 yards and a touchdown, his third of the season, against the [[New York Jets]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Mayer |first=Larry |date=October 28, 2018 |title=Bears turn on Jets to snap skid |url=https://www.chicagobears.com/news/game-recap-bears-beat-jets-to-snap-two-game-skid |access-date=September 19, 2019 |website=Chicagobears.com}}</ref> In Week 10 against the [[Detroit Lions]], Miller caught five passes for 122 yards and a touchdown. The Bears won the game by a score of 34–22.<ref>{{Cite web |date=November 11, 2018 |title=Bears' Anthony Miller: Explodes for career-best effort |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/football/news/bears-anthony-miller-explodes-for-career-best-effort/ |access-date=December 5, 2018 |website=CBSSports.com |language=en}}</ref>

In Week 13 against the [[New York Giants]], Miller caught the game-tying touchdown pass in regulation on a trick play: quarterback [[Chase Daniel]] tossed the ball to tight end [[Trey Burton]], who then tossed it to running back [[Tarik Cohen]], who threw it to Miller for the touchdown. Miller's touchdown sent the game into overtime, tied 27–27. Unfortunately, the Bears lost to the Giants in overtime 30–27 after the Bears failed to convert a fourth down in overtime.<ref>{{Cite web |date=December 2, 2018 |title=Bears halfback Tarik Cohen has career day in loss to Giants |url=https://www.foxsports.com/nfl/story/bears-halfback-tarik-cohen-has-career-day-in-loss-to-giants-120218 |access-date=December 3, 2018 |website=[[Foxsports.com]] |agency=Associated Press}}</ref>

In Week 16 against the [[San Francisco 49ers]], Miller was ejected after he got in a fight with safety [[Marcell Harris]].  Miller attacked Harris after he hit quarterback [[Mitchell Trubisky]] as he was sliding to the ground. In addition, fellow Bears wide receiver [[Josh Bellamy]] and 49ers cornerback [[Richard Sherman (American football)|Richard Sherman]] were ejected from the game.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Finley |first=Patrick |date=December 23, 2018 |title=Bears WRs Anthony Miller, Josh Bellamy ejected in fight with 49ers |url=https://chicago.suntimes.com/sports/bears-wrs-anthony-miller-josh-bellamy-ejected-in-fight-with-49ers/ |access-date=January 29, 2019 |website=Chicago Sun-Times |language=en}}</ref> Before he was ejected, he had three catches for 24 yards and a touchdown. The Bears won the game 14–9.<ref name="2018 Game Log">{{Cite web |title=Anthony Miller 2018 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/M/MillAn02.htm |access-date=January 29, 2019 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

Miller finished his rookie season with 33 catches for 423 yards and seven touchdowns.<ref name="2018 Game Log" /> His seven touchdowns led the team and were the most by a Bears rookie since [[Willie Gault]] had seven in 1983; he also ranked second in the league among rookie receivers behind the [[Atlanta Falcons]]' [[Calvin Ridley]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Mayer |first=Larry |date=February 6, 2019 |title=Bears 2018 position review: Receiver |url=https://www.chicagobears.com/news/bears-2018-position-review-receiver |access-date=February 11, 2019 |publisher=[[Chicago Bears]]}}</ref> He received an overall grade of 60.6 from [[Pro Football Focus]] in 2018, which ranked as the 92nd-highest grade among all qualifying wide receivers.<ref>{{Cite web |last=<!--Not stated--> |title=Pro Football Focus: Anthony Miller |url=https://www.profootballfocus.com/nfl/players/anthony-miller/48160 |access-date=March 31, 2019 |website=profootballfocus.com}}</ref>

====2019====
[[File:Anthony Miller (wide receiver, born 1994).JPG|thumb|Miller in the 2019 NFL season]]
Against the Lions in Week 13, Miller finished with a career-high nine catches for 140 receiving yards as the Bears won 24–20.<ref>{{Cite web |date=November 28, 2019 |title=Trubisky's 3rd TD pass lifts Bears to 24–20 win over Lions |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/recap?gameId=401128015 |access-date=November 28, 2019 |website=ESPN.com |agency=Associated Press}}</ref> In the following week's game against the [[Dallas Cowboys]], Miller caught three passes for 42 yards and his first touchdown of the season in the 31–24 win.<ref>{{Cite web |date=December 5, 2019 |title=Mitchell Trubisky helps Bears beat Cowboys 31–24 |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/recap?gameId=401127871 |access-date=December 5, 2019 |website=ESPN.com |agency=Associated Press}}</ref> In Week 15 against the Packers, Miller caught nine passes for 118 yards and a touchdown during the 21–13 loss.<ref>{{Cite web |date=December 15, 2019 |title=Jones scores twice, Packers complete season sweep of Bears |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/recap?gameId=401128031 |access-date=December 15, 2019 |website=ESPN.com |agency=Associated Press}}</ref> Overall, Miller finished the 2019 season with 52 receptions for 656 receiving yards and two receiving touchdowns.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Anthony Miller 2019 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/M/MillAn02/gamelog/2019/ |access-date=March 23, 2020 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

====2020====
In the 2020 season opener against the Lions, Miller scored the go-ahead touchdown with 1:55 remaining on a 27-yard reception from Trubisky; Miller's assignment, a [[fly route]] from the right slot receiver position, was the same pattern he ran in the 2019 Thanksgiving game that resulted in a 32-yard catch. Miller ended the 27–23 victory with four catches for 76 yards.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Finley |first=Patrick |date=September 13, 2020 |title=Bears recycle Thanksgiving play for Anthony Miller TD |url=https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears/2020/9/13/21435487/bears-anthony-miller-mitch-trubisky-touchdown-catch-thanksgiving-go-route-lions-tony-mcrae-week-1 |access-date=September 13, 2020 |website=[[Chicago Sun-Times]]}}</ref>
In Week 3 against the [[Atlanta Falcons]], Miller caught a 28-yard touchdown pass late in the fourth quarter to help the Bears come back to win the game 30–26.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Chicago Bears at Atlanta Falcons – September 27th, 2020 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202009270atl.htm |access-date=September 29, 2020 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> He finished the 2020 season with 49 receptions for 485 receiving yards and two receiving touchdowns.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Anthony Miller 2020 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/M/MillAn02/gamelog/2020/ |access-date=November 20, 2022 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> Miller was ejected from the [[2020–21 NFL playoffs#NFC: New Orleans Saints 21, Chicago Bears 9|Wild Card Round]] of the [[2020–21 NFL playoffs]] for hitting [[New Orleans Saints]] cornerback [[C. J. Gardner-Johnson]]. Miller caught two passes for 22 yards prior to being disqualified from the game.<ref>{{Cite web |last=DeArdo |first=Bryan |date=January 11, 2021 |title=Bears' Anthony Miller ejected during wild-card playoff game vs. Saints after scuffle with C.J. Gardner-Johnson |url=https://www.cbssports.com/nfl/news/bears-anthony-miller-ejected-during-wild-card-playoff-game-vs-saints-after-scuffle-with-c-j-gardner-johnson/ |access-date=January 11, 2021 |website=CBS Sports}}</ref>

===Houston Texans===
On July 26, 2021, Miller was traded to the [[Houston Texans]] along with a 2022 seventh-round pick for a 2022 fifth-round pick.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Mayer |first=Larry |date=July 26, 2021 |title=Roster Move: Bears trade Miller to Texans |url=https://www.chicagobears.com/news/roster-move-bears-trade-miller-to-texans |access-date=November 20, 2022 |website=ChicagoBears.com}}</ref> He scored his first touchdown as a Texan in Week 3 against the Panthers.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Carolina Panthers at Houston Texans – September 23rd, 2021 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202109230htx.htm |access-date=November 20, 2022 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> He played in two games before being released on October 6, 2021.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Lane |first=Mark |date=October 6, 2021 |title=Texans to release WR Anthony Miller |url=https://texanswire.usatoday.com/2021/10/06/texans-release-anthony-miller/ |access-date=November 20, 2022 |website=Texans Wire|publisher=USA Today}}</ref>

===Pittsburgh Steelers===
On October 12, 2021, Miller was signed to the [[practice squad]] of the [[Pittsburgh Steelers]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bryan |first=Dave |date=October 12, 2021 |title=Report: Steelers Sign WR Anthony Miller, DL Isaiah Mack To Practice Squad |url=https://steelersdepot.com/2021/10/report-steelers-sign-wr-anthony-miller-dl-isaiah-mack-to-practice-squad/ |access-date=November 20, 2022 |website=Steelers Depot}}</ref> He was elevated to the active roster from the practice squad on November 27, 2021.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Varley |first=Teresa |date=November 27, 2021 |title=Steelers make moves, place two on IR |url=https://www.steelers.com/news/steelers-make-moves-place-two-on-ir |access-date=November 20, 2022 |website=Steelers.com}}</ref> He signed a reserve/future contract with the Steelers on January 24, 2022.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Hartman |first=Jeff |date=January 24, 2022 |title=Steelers sign wide receiver Anthony Miller to a Reserve/Future contract |url=https://www.behindthesteelcurtain.com/2022/1/24/22899769/steelers-sign-wide-receiver-anthony-miller-to-a-reserve-future-contract-nfl-news-update-rumors |access-date=November 20, 2022 |website=Behind the Steel Curtain |publisher=SB Nation |language=en}}</ref>

On August 16, 2022, Miller was placed on [[injured reserve]] with a season-ending shoulder injury.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Varley |first=Teresa |date=August 16, 2022 |title=Steelers make roster moves on Tuesday |url=https://www.steelers.com/news/steelers-sign-dunkle-make-additional-moves |access-date=November 20, 2022 |website=Steelers.com}}</ref>

On January 17, 2023, Miller signed a one-year contract extension with the Steelers.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Varley |first=Teresa |date=January 17, 2023 |title=Miller signed to one-year contract |url=https://www.steelers.com/news/miller-signed-to-one-year-contract |access-date=May 17, 2023 |website=Steelers.com}}</ref> He was released on June 20, 2023.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Varley |first=Teresa |date=June 20, 2023 |title=Steelers sign Kwiatkoski and Sunahara |url=https://www.steelers.com/news/steelers-sign-kwiatkoski-and-sunahara |access-date=February 16, 2024 |website=Steelers.com}}</ref>

===San Francisco 49ers===
On August 22, 2023, Miller signed with the 49ers.<ref>{{Cite web |date=August 22, 2023 |title=49ers Sign WR Anthony Miller; Waive a Wide Receiver |url=https://www.49ers.com/news/49ers-sign-wr-anthony-miller-waive-a-wide-receiver |access-date=February 16, 2024 |website=49ers.com}}</ref> He was released on August 29, 2023.<ref>{{Cite web |date=August 29, 2023 |title=49ers Announce Moves for Initial 53-Man Roster |url=https://www.49ers.com/news/49ers-announce-moves-for-initial-53-man-roster |access-date=February 16, 2024 |website=49ers.com}}</ref>

===Indianapolis Colts===
On October 11, 2023, the [[Indianapolis Colts]] signed Miller to their practice squad.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Stankevitz |first=JJ |date=October 11, 2023 |title=Colts place QB Anthony Richardson on injured reserve, sign G Ike Boettger to 53-man roster from practice squad; sign WR Anthony Miller, QB Kellen Mond to practice squad, release WR Juwann Winfree from practice squad |url=https://www.colts.com/news/anthony-richardson-injured-reserve-quarterback-kellen-mond-signed-practice-squad |access-date=February 16, 2024 |website=Colts.com}}</ref> He was released on October 17, 2023.<ref>{{Cite web |date=October 17, 2023 |title=Colts sign WR Juwann Winfree; restore G Jack Anderson to practice squad; sign two players to practice squad; release three players from the practice squad |url=https://www.colts.com/news/colts-sign-wr-juwann-winfree-restore-g-jack-anderson-to-practice-squad-sign-two- |access-date=February 16, 2024 |website=Colts.com}}</ref>

===Kansas City Chiefs===
On January 23, 2024, Miller signed a reserve/future contract with the [[Kansas City Chiefs]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Conner |first=Matt |date=January 24, 2024 |title=Chiefs news: Anthony Miller officially signs futures deal |url=https://arrowheadaddict.com/posts/chiefs-news-anthony-miller-officially-signs-futures-deal-01hmwm3vvn0j |access-date=February 14, 2024 |website=Arrowhead Addict}}</ref> He was released on May 3, 2024.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Williams |first=Charean |author-link=Charean Williams |date=May 3, 2024 |title=Chiefs' roster moves include the release of WR Anthony Miller |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/profootballtalk/rumor-mill/news/chiefs-roster-moves-include-the-release-of-wr-anthony-miller |access-date=May 3, 2024 |website=NBC Sports}}</ref>

===Baltimore Ravens===
On August 11, 2024, Miller signed with the [[Baltimore Ravens]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Brown |first=Clifton |date=August 11, 2024 |title=Ravens Make Several Roster Moves |url=https://www.baltimoreravens.com/news/ravens-sign-anthony-miller-jack-browning-2024-training-camp |access-date=2024-12-27 |website=BaltimoreRavens.com}}</ref> He was released on August 27, and re-signed to the practice squad.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Brown |first=Clifton |date=August 27, 2024 |title=Ravens Make Cuts, Set 53-Man Roster |url=https://www.baltimoreravens.com/news/ravens-53-man-roster-cuts-2024-pepe-williams-devin-leary-dayton-wade-anthony-miller-qadir-ismail |access-date=2024-12-27 |website=BaltimoreRavens.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Mink |first=Ryan |date=August 28, 2024 |title=Ravens Sign 15 Players to Practice Squad |url=https://www.baltimoreravens.com/news/baltimore-ravens-news-practice-squad-signing-transactions-2024-initial |access-date=2024-12-27 |website=BaltimoreRavens.com}}</ref> In Week 17 against the Texans, he had his first catch since the 2021 season.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Anthony Miller Career Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/M/MillAn02/gamelog/ |access-date=2025-02-04 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> Miller was elevated to the active roster for the Ravens' playoff game against the Buffalo Bills, a 27–25 loss.<ref name="f437">{{cite web | title=Ravens elevate WR Anthony Miller from the practice squad with Zay Flowers doubtful | website=AP News | date=2025-01-18 | url=https://apnews.com/article/baltimore-ravens-anthony-miller-e299b6459b37cd7b3581f42826e997e8 | access-date=2025-02-04}}</ref> He signed a reserve/future contract on January 21, 2025.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Mink |first=Ryan |date=January 21, 2025 |title=Ravens Sign 11 Players to Reserve/Future Contracts |url=https://www.baltimoreravens.com/news/ravens-reserve-future-contracts-2025 |access-date=2025-02-04 |website=BaltimoreRavens.com}}</ref>

On August 26, 2025, Miller was released by the Ravens as part of final roster cuts and re-signed to the practice squad the next day.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Mink |first1=Ryan |title=Ravens' Initial Practice Squad Is Set |url=https://www.baltimoreravens.com/news/ravens-practice-squad-2025-tyler-huntley |website=baltimoreravens.com |access-date=1 September 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Mink |first1=Ryan |date=August 27, 2025 |title=5 Takeaways From Ravens Roster Cuts |url=https://www.baltimoreravens.com/news/ravens-roster-cuts-53-takeaways-2025 |access-date=1 September 2025 |website=Baltimore Ravens}}</ref> He was released on September 24.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Petry |first1=Josh |date=September 24, 2025 |title=Ravens cut two veterans after signing new defensive talent |url=https://touchdownwire.usatoday.com/story/sports/nfl/touchdown/2025/09/24/the-baltimore-ravens-had-parted-ways-with-two-veterans-in-favor-of-new-signings/86336325007/ |access-date=25 September 2025 |website=Touchdown Wire|publisher=USA Today}}</ref>

'''Anthony Dwayne Phillips''' (born October 5, 1970) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[defensive back]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) for the [[Atlanta Falcons]] and [[Minnesota Vikings]]. He played [[college football]] for the [[Texas A&M–Kingsville Javelinas football|Texas A&M–Kingsville Javelinas]].<ref name = "MLive">{{cite web|url=http://www.mlive.com/news/kalamazoo/index.ssf/2011/12/former_nfl_player_kalamazoo_re.html|title=Former NFL player, Kalamazoo resident finds satisfaction in a life of ups and downs|first=Jef Rietsma Special to the Kalamazoo|last=Gazette|website=MLive.com|date=December 25, 2011 }}</ref> He also played in the [[Arena Football League]] (AFL) for the [[Grand Rapids Rampage]] and [[Buffalo Destroyers]], winning the [[Arena Bowl]] with Grand Rapids in his first season there.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.justsportsstats.com/footballstatsindex.php?player_id=phillant001 |title=Anthony Phillips Statistics on StatsCrew.com |website=www.StatsCrew.com |access-date=2020-01-25}}</ref>

==Professional career==
After attending [[Texas A&M–Kingsville]], Phillips was selected by the [[Atlanta Falcons]] in [[1994 NFL draft|1994]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=1994 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/1994/draft.htm |access-date=2023-03-31 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> He became a rising star with the Falcons, but in his second season, he suffered a gruesome leg injury. During a game against the [[Buffalo Bills]], Phillips intercepted a pass thrown by Buffalo quarterback [[Jim Kelly]], catching the ball at the Atlanta 2-yard line, and was on his way to returning the ball for a defensive touchdown. However, after 43 yards, Kelly himself caught up to Phillips and tackled him while he was running (in bounds) down the side line, with the latter suffering a [[compound fracture]] to both his [[tibia]] and [[fibula]] on his right leg upon landing awkwardly on it.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/734757-20-most-gruesome-injuries-in-nfl-history#slide14 |title=NFL: 20 Most Gruesome Injuries in NFL History |last=Van Wie |first=Dan |website=Bleacher Report |language=en |access-date=2020-01-25}}</ref> Phillips was required to stay on his back for a month in order for the bones to heal, and Kelly has since apologized for the injury.<ref name = "MLive" />

Phillips was cut after one additional season with the Falcons. He later signed with the [[Minnesota Vikings]] in 1998, but his season ended with a torn ACL. After the season, he played two seasons in the [[Arena Football League]], helping the [[Grand Rapids Rampage]] win [[ArenaBowl XV]], before retiring.<ref name = "MLive" />

==Personal life==
Raised in [[Galveston, Texas]], Phillips has four children and later settled in [[Kalamazoo, Michigan]]. He was diagnosed with kidney failure, stemming from legal steroid usage during his football career.<ref name = "MLive" />Before Death, He face the pain Gracefully
