'''Anthony Nelson''' (born March 4, 1997) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[linebacker]] for the [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Iowa Hawkeyes football|Iowa Hawkeyes]], and was selected by the Buccaneers in the fourth round of the [[2019 NFL draft]].

==Early life==
Anthony Nelson was born on March 4, 1997, in [[Urbandale, Iowa]].<ref name="pfr">{{cite web | url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/N/NelsAn01.htm | title=Anthony Nelson | publisher=[[Pro Football Reference]] | accessdate=20 March 2026}}</ref> He attended [[Waukee High School]] in [[Waukee, Iowa]].<ref name="pfr"/>

==College career==
Nelson signed with the [[University of Iowa]] on February 4, 2015.<ref>{{cite new |title=Future Hawkeye Anthony Nelson leads swarm of Waukee signees |url=https://www.desmoinesregister.com/story/sports/high-school/2015/02/04/waukee-trevor-allen-anthony-nelson-signing-day/22861749/ |newspaper=[[The Des Moines Register]]|date=February 4, 2015 |access-date=November 30, 2025}}</ref> He redshirted during the [[2015 Iowa Hawkeyes football team|Hawkeyes historic 2015 season]].

As a redshirt freshman at Iowa, Nelson played in all 13 games with one start. He earned Big Ten Freshman of the Week honors after collecting 2.5 sacks in a win over Miami (OH)<ref name="b1g-pow-week1">{{cite web |title=J.T. Barrett highlights Week 1 Big Ten Players of the Week |url=http://btn.com/2016/09/05/j-t-barrett-highlights-week-1-big-ten-players-of-the-week/ |work=[[Big Ten Network]]|date=September 5, 2016 |access-date=November 30, 2025}}</ref> {{ndash}} his first game as a Hawkeye {{ndash}} and finished the season second on the team in sacks and tackles for loss. Nelson's first career start came in a 42{{ndash}}3 win over in-state rival Iowa State.

During his sophomore season, Nelson started all 13 games and led the team with 7.5 sacks. He also had four pass break-ups, two forced fumbles and a blocked field goal. After the season, Nelson was named third-team All-Big Ten by the media and honorable mention by league coaches. He made several key plays, including two sacks and a forced fumble, to help the Hawkeyes win the [[2017 Pinstripe Bowl]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Iowa rallies to beat Boston College 27-20 in Pinstripe Bowl |url=https://collegefootball.ap.org/article/iowa-rallies-beat-boston-college-27-20-pinstripe-bowl |work=[[Associated Press]]|date=December 27, 2017 |access-date=November 30, 2025}}</ref>

Nelson again started all 13 games as a junior, establishing career bests for sacks (9.5) and tackles for loss (13.5). He was Big Ten Defensive Player of the Week after wins over Minnesota and Nebraska<ref>{{cite web |title=Anthony Nelson Named B1G Player of the Week |url=https://hawkeyesports.com/news/2018/11/26/football-anthony-nelson-named-b1g-player-of-the-week |work=[[Iowa Hawkeyes|University of Iowa Athletics]]|date=November 26, 2018 |access-date=November 30, 2025}}</ref>, and recovered a fumble for a touchdown in a shutout win over Maryland.<ref>{{cite web |title=No. 19 Iowa Pummels Maryland 23–0 For 3rd Straight Win |url=https://collegefootball.ap.org/article/no-19-iowa-pummels-maryland-23-0-3rd-straight-win |work=[[Associated Press]]|date=October 20, 2018 |access-date=November 30, 2025}}</ref> After the season, Nelson was named second-team All-Big Ten by media and third-team by coaches.

Despite having one year of eligibility remaining, Nelson declared for the NFL Draft after his junior season at Iowa.<ref>{{cite news |title=Iowa’s Anthony Nelson enters NFL Draft |url=https://www.thegazette.com/hawkeye-football/iowas-anthony-nelson-enters-nfl-draft/ |publisher=[[The Gazette (Cedar Rapids, Iowa)|The Gazette]] |date=January 7, 2019 |access-date=November 30, 2025}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Morehouse |first=Marc |date=March 2, 2019 |title=Iowa's Anthony Nelson knew it was time for the NFL |url=https://www.thegazette.com/subject/sports/hawkeyes/iowa-football/anthony-nelson-iowa-defensive-end-nfl-draft-2019-combine-20190302 |access-date=February 18, 2023 |website=The Gazette}}</ref> He and former Hawkeye teammate [[A. J. Epenesa]] are the only players in school history to finish their careers on the [[Iowa Hawkeyes football statistical leaders#Sacks|school's top ten sacks list]] while only playing three years at Iowa.

Nelson was selected by the [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]] in the fourth round, 107th overall, of the [[2019 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Vitali |first=Carmen |date=April 27, 2019 |title=Buccaneers Select Anthony Nelson in Fourth Round of the 2019 NFL Draft |url=https://www.buccaneers.com/news/buccaneers-select-anthony-nelson-in-fourth-round-of-the-2019-nfl-draft |access-date=March 15, 2021 |website=Buccaneers.com}}</ref>

In Week 16 of the 2020 season against the [[Detroit Lions]], Nelson recorded his first career sack on [[David Blough]] during the 47–7 win.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Detroit Lions – December 26th, 2020 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202012260det.htm |access-date=December 30, 2020 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> Nelson was a part of the [[Super Bowl LV]] champion Buccaneers. He recorded four solo tackles across the postseason, including one in the Super Bowl.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Anthony Nelson 2020 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/N/NelsAn01/gamelog/2020/ |access-date=March 15, 2021 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Patra |first=Kevin |date=February 7, 2017 |title=What we learned from Buccaneers win over Chiefs in Super Bowl LV |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/what-we-learned-from-buccaneers-win-over-chiefs-in-super-bowl-lv |access-date=March 15, 2021 |website=NFL.com |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Super Bowl LV – Tampa Bay Buccaneers vs. Kansas City Chiefs – February 7th, 2021 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202102070tam.htm |access-date=March 15, 2021 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

On March 16, 2023, Nelson signed a two-year contract extension with the Buccaneers.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Smith |first=Scott |date=March 16, 2023 |title=Anthony Nelson Agrees to Terms with Buccaneers |url=https://www.buccaneers.com/news/anthony-nelson-agrees-terms-free-agency-2023 |access-date=March 13, 2024 |website=Buccaneers.com}}</ref>

On March 11, 2025, Nelson re-signed with Tampa Bay on a two-year, $10 million contract.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Anthony Nelson Lands Third Contract with Buccaneers|url=https://www.buccaneers.com/news/anthony-nelson-lands-third-contract-buccaneers|access-date=March 17, 2025|website=buccaneers.com|language=en}}</ref> In Week 8, Nelson intercepted a pass from [[Spencer Rattler]] and returned it for a three-yard touchdown. He also recorded two sacks and a forced fumble in the 23-3 win over the [[2025 New Orleans Saints season|New Orleans Saints]], earning NFC Defensive Player of the Week.<ref>{{cite web|title=Bills RB James Cook, Packers QB Jordan Love highlight Players of the Week|url=https://www.nfl.com/news/players-of-the-week-2025-week-8-james-cook-jordan-love|author=Kownack, Bobby|website=NFL.com|date=October 29, 2025}}</ref>

'''Anthony Rush''' (born September 1, 1996) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[nose tackle]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL).<ref name=":0">{{cite web |title=Anthony Rush (DT): Bio, News, Stats & more |url=https://www.atlantafalcons.com/team/players-roster/anthony-rush/ |website=www.atlantafalcons.com |access-date=2 May 2022}}</ref> After playing [[college football]] for the [[UAB Blazers football|UAB Blazers]], he was signed by the [[Philadelphia Eagles]] as an [[undrafted free agent]] in 2019. He was also a member of the [[Oakland Raiders]], [[Seattle Seahawks]], [[Chicago Bears]], [[Green Bay Packers]], [[Tennessee Titans]], [[Atlanta Falcons]], and [[Dallas Cowboys]].

== Early life ==
Rush is a native of [[Raleigh, North Carolina]].<ref name=":0" /> He attended [[Cary High School]].<ref name=":0" /> He played both defense and offense for his high school team, earning first-team All Southwest Wake Athletic Conference honors as a junior.<ref name=":0" />

==College career==
Because of problems with academics coming out of high school Rush spent his first two years of college at [[Northeast Mississippi Community College]] where he recorded 73 [[Tackle (football move)#Gridiron football|tackles]] and 4 [[Quarterback sack|sacks]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Anthony Rush UAB |url=https://uabsports.com/sports/football/roster/anthony-rush/5499 |publisher=UAB Athletics}}</ref> In his two years at the [[University of Alabama at Birmingham]], Rush recorded 77 tackles (20 for loss), 2 sacks and an [[interception]] returned for a [[touchdown]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Raiders hope they have a steal in undrafted rookie DT Anthony Rush |date=August 22, 2019 |url=https://www.sfchronicle.com/raiders/amp/Raiders-hope-they-have-a-steal-in-undrafted-14368824.php |publisher=San Francisco Chronicles}}</ref>

===Philadelphia Eagles===
Rush signed with the [[Philadelphia Eagles]] as an [[undrafted free agent]] on April 28, 2019.<ref>{{Cite web |last=McPherson, Chris |date=May 9, 2019 |title=Eagles sign entire 2019 draft class and 10 undrafted free agents |url=https://www.philadelphiaeagles.com/news/eagles-sign-entire-2019-draft-class-and-undrafted-free-agents |website=PhiladelphiaEagles.com}}</ref> He was waived on July 27.<ref>{{Cite news |last=McPherson, Chris |date=July 27, 2019 |title=Eagles sign CB Orlando Scandrick |work=PhiladelphiaEagles.com |url=https://www.philadelphiaeagles.com/news/eagles-sign-cb-orlando-scandrick |access-date=October 21, 2019}}</ref>

===Oakland Raiders===
Rush signed with the [[Oakland Raiders]] on August 1, 2019.<ref>{{Cite news |date=August 1, 2019 |title=Raiders sign defensive tackle Anthony Rush |work=Raiders.com |url=https://www.raiders.com/news/raiders-sign-defensive-tackle-anthony-rush |access-date=October 21, 2019}}</ref> He was waived during final roster cuts on August 31, 2019,<ref>{{Cite news |date=August 31, 2019 |title=Raiders announce transactions – 8.31.19 |work=Raiders.com |url=https://www.raiders.com/news/raiders-announce-transactions-8-31-19 |access-date=October 21, 2019}}</ref> but was re-signed to the team's [[practice squad]] on September 2.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Straub, Luke |date=September 2, 2019 |title=Raiders' initial practice squad is set for 2019 season |work=USA Today |url=https://raiderswire.usatoday.com/2019/09/02/raiders-initial-practice-squad-is-set-for-2019-season/ |access-date=October 21, 2019}}</ref>

===Philadelphia Eagles (second stint)===
On October 21, 2019, Rush was signed by the Eagles off the Raiders' practice squad.<ref>{{Cite news |last=McPherson, Chris |date=October 21, 2019 |title=Eagles agree to sign DT Anthony Rush, release CB Orlando Scandrick and DT Akeem Spence |work=PhiladelphiaEagles.com |url=https://www.philadelphiaeagles.com/news/eagles-agree-to-sign-anthony-rush-release-orlando-scandrick-akeem-spence |access-date=October 21, 2019}}</ref> He was waived on September 5, 2020.<ref>{{Cite web |last=McPherson, Chris |date=September 5, 2020 |title=Eagles announce initial 53-man roster |url=https://www.philadelphiaeagles.com/news/eagles-announce-initial-53-man-roster |website=PhiladelphiaEagles.com}}</ref>

===Seattle Seahawks===
On September 9, 2020, Rush was signed to the [[Seattle Seahawks]] practice squad.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Boyle, John |date=September 9, 2020 |title=Seahawks Sign WR John Ursua & DT Anthony Rush To Practice Squad |url=https://www.seahawks.com/news/seahawks-sign-wr-john-ursua-dt-anthony-rush-to-practice-squad |website=Seahawks.com}}</ref> He was elevated to the active roster on September 19 for the team's Week 2 game against the [[New England Patriots]], and reverted to the practice squad after the game.<ref>{{Cite news |date=September 19, 2020 |title=Anthony Rush Elevated From Practice Squad For Week 2 vs. Patriots |work=Seahawks.com |url=https://www.seahawks.com/news/anthony-rush-elevated-from-practice-squad-for-week-2-vs-patriots |access-date=October 5, 2020}}</ref> He was promoted to the active roster on September 23.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Boyle |first=John |date=September 23, 2020 |title=Seahawks Promoted Linden Stephens & Anthony Rush From Practice Squad; Place Three Players On IR |work=Seahawks.com |url=https://www.seahawks.com/news/seahawks-promoted-linden-stephens-anthony-rush-from-practice-squad-place-three-p}}</ref> He was waived on October 27, 2020.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Condotta, Bob |date=October 27, 2020 |title=The Seahawks waive Anthony Rush, while the Cowboys trade Everson Griffen to Detroit, not Seattle |work=The Seattle Times |url=https://www.seattletimes.com/sports/seahawks/the-seahawks-waive-anthony-rush-while-the-cowboys-trade-everson-griffen-to-detroit-not-seattle/ |access-date=November 9, 2020}}</ref>

===Green Bay Packers===
On November 25, 2020, Rush was claimed off waivers by the [[Green Bay Packers]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=November 30, 2020 |title=Packers claim DL Anthony Rush off of waivers |url=https://www.packers.com/news/packers-claim-dl-anthony-rush-off-of-waivers |publisher=packers.com}}</ref> He was waived by the Packers on December 31, 2020,<ref>{{Cite web |date=December 31, 2020 |title=Packers claim DL Damon Harrison off of waivers from the Seahawks |url=https://www.packers.com/news/packers-claim-dl-damon-harrison-off-of-waivers-from-the-seahawks |website=Packers.com}}</ref> and re-signed to the practice squad two days later.<ref>{{Cite web |date=January 2, 2021 |title=Packers place David Bakhtiari on IR |url=https://www.packers.com/news/packers-place-t-david-bakhtiari-on-injured-reserve |website=Packers.com}}</ref> On January 25, 2021, Rush signed a reserve/futures contract with the Packers.<ref>{{Cite web |date=January 25, 2021 |title=Packers sign 10 free agents |url=https://www.packers.com/news/packers-sign-10-free-agents-x1386 |website=Green Bay Packers |accessdate=January 25, 2021 |archive-date=January 26, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210126034530/https://www.packers.com/news/packers-sign-10-free-agents-x1386 |url-status=dead }}</ref> He was waived on June 10, 2021.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Packers sign QB Jake Dolegala |url=https://www.packers.com/news/packers-sign-qb-jake-dolegala |access-date=June 10, 2021 |publisher=packers.com}}</ref>

===Tennessee Titans===
On July 26, 2021, Rush signed with the [[Tennessee Titans]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=July 26, 2021 |title=Titans add Kyle Peko, Anthony Rush, waive Bruce Hector |url=https://titanswire.usatoday.com/2021/07/26/titans-add-kyle-peko-anthony-rush-waive-bruce-hector/ |website=USAToday.com}}</ref> He was released on September 21, 2021.<ref>{{cite web|title=Titans Release Safety Bradley McDougald, DL Anthony Rush|url=https://www.tennesseetitans.com/news/titans-release-safety-bradley-mcdougald-dl-anthony-rush|author=Wyatt, Jim|website=TennesseeTitans.com|date=September 21, 2021}}</ref>

===Atlanta Falcons===
On September 23, 2021, Rush signed with the practice squad of the [[Atlanta Falcons]].<ref>{{cite web|title= Falcons Sign Mountain of a Man for DL |url= https://www.si.com/nfl/falcons/news/atlanta-falcons-sign-former-philadelphia-eagle-anthony-rush |website=SI.com|date=September 23, 2021 |accessdate=September 25, 2021}}</ref> On November 8, 2021, Rush was promoted to the active roster.<ref>{{cite web|title=What to make of the moves: Falcons sign defensive lineman Anthony Rush, release Deadrin Senat|url=https://www.atlantafalcons.com/news/what-to-make-of-the-moves-falcons-sign-anthony-rush-release-deadrin-senat|website=AtlantaFalcons.com|date=November 8, 2021}}</ref> Rush made his first career NFL start in Week 11 against the New England Patriots.

On March 17, 2022, Rush signed a one-year contract with the Falcons.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Falcons' Anthony Rush: Returns to Atlanta |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/football/news/falcons-anthony-rush-returns-to-atlanta/ |access-date=2022-03-18 |website=CBSSports.com |date=March 17, 2022 |language=en}}</ref> He started the first four games before getting waived on October 6, 2022.<ref>{{cite web|title=Falcons release veteran defensive tackle|url=https://www.atlantafalcons.com/news/anthony-rush-falcons-release-veteran-defensive-tackle-buccaneers|author=Bair, Scott|website=AtlantaFalcons.com|date=October 6, 2022}}</ref>

===Philadelphia Eagles (third stint)===
On November 24, 2022, Rush was signed to the Eagles practice squad. He was released on December 6.<ref>{{cite web|title=Roster Moves: Eagles free spots on both the 53-man roster and practice squad|url=https://www.philadelphiaeagles.com/news/roster-moves-eagles-free-spots-on-both-the-53-man-roster-and-practice-squad|website=PhiladelphiaEagles.com|date=December 6, 2022}}</ref>

===Dallas Cowboys===
On December 14, 2022, Rush was signed to the Dallas Cowboys practice squad, after [[defensive tackle]] [[Johnathan Hankins]] suffered a pectoral injury. On January 30, 2023, he was released.

'''Anthony McFarland Jr.''' (born March 4, 1998) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[running back]] for the [[Birmingham Stallions (2022)|Birmingham Stallions]] of the [[United Football League (2024)|United Football League]] (UFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Maryland Terrapins football|Maryland Terrapins]], and was selected by the [[Pittsburgh Steelers]] in the fourth round of the [[2020 NFL draft]].

==Early life==
McFarland attended Ernest Everett Just Middle School in [[Lake Arbor, Maryland]], before attending [[DeMatha Catholic High School]] in [[Hyattsville, Maryland]]. He did not play football his senior season of high school due to injury.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Giannotto |first=Mark |date=August 18, 2016 |title=DeMatha loses RB Anthony McFarland to a broken fibula just before the season |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/highschools/dematha-loses-rb-anthony-mcfarland-to-a-broken-fibula-just-the-before-season/2016/08/18/43543960-657c-11e6-be4e-23fc4d4d12b4_story.html |via=www.washingtonpost.com}}</ref> Despite this he was still an [[Under Armour All-American Game|Under Armour All-American]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2016-11-02 |title=Anthony McFarland Jr. receives Under Armour All-America jersey |url=https://usatodayhss.com/2016/anthony-mcfarland-jr-receives-under-armour-all-america-jersey |access-date=2023-10-29 |website=USA TODAY High School Sports |language=en-US}}</ref> He committed to the [[University of Maryland]] to play [[college football]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Bogage |first=Jacob |title=DeMatha running back Anthony McFarland commits to Maryland |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/news/recruiting-insider/wp/2017/01/27/dematha-running-back-anthony-mcfarland-commits-to-maryland/ |newspaper=Washington Post}}</ref> At DeMatha, he was a teammate of [[defensive end]] [[Chase Young]], who was later selected second overall in the [[2020 NFL draft]] by the [[Washington Football Team]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Hailey |first=Peter |title=Terps RB Anthony McFarland practiced against Chase Young in high school. It wasn't fun |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/washington/redskins/terps-rb-anthony-mcfarland-practiced-against-chase-young-high-school-it-wasnt-fun |access-date=May 19, 2020 |website=NBC Sports}}</ref>

==College career==
McFarland Jr. redshirted his first year at Maryland in 2017. He played for the first time in two years in 2018.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Markus |first=Don |title=With two straight 100-yard games, Maryland's Anthony McFarland starting to live up to the hype |url=https://www.baltimoresun.com/sports/terps/bs-sp-anthony-mcfarland-0926-story.html |website=baltimoresun.com|date=September 26, 2018 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Giambalvo |first=Emily |date=September 27, 2018 |title=Maryland's Anthony McFarland has emerged – to the tune of 10.8 yards per carry |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/2018/09/27/after-two-years-sideline-anthony-mcfarland-has-emerged-key-piece-marylands-offense/ |access-date=September 28, 2020 |newspaper=Washington Post}}</ref> He started five of 12 games, rushing for 1,034 yards on 131 carries with four [[touchdown]]s. In 2019, he rushed for 614 yards on 114 carries and eight touchdowns. After the season, he entered the [[2020 NFL draft]], forgoing his final two seasons.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Alper |first=Josh |date=December 3, 2019 |title=Maryland RB Anthony McFarland Jr. declares for 2020 draft |url=https://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2019/12/03/maryland-rb-anthony-mcfarland-jr-declares-for-2020-draft/ |access-date=September 28, 2020 |website=ProFootballTalk}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Giambalvo |first=Emily  |date=December 3, 2019 |title=Anthony McFarland Jr. will enter NFL draft, skipping his final two seasons at Maryland |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/2019/12/03/anthony-mcfarland-jr-nfl-draft-maryland-football/ |access-date=September 28, 2020 |work=Washington Post}}</ref>

=== Pittsburgh Steelers ===
McFarland was selected by the [[Pittsburgh Steelers]] in the fourth round of the 2020 NFL draft.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Varley |first=Teresa |date=April 25, 2020 |title=Steelers select McFarland in the fourth round |url=https://www.steelers.com/news/steelers-select-mcfarland-in-the-fourth-round |access-date=September 28, 2020 |website=Steelers.com}}</ref> He made his NFL debut in Week 3 of the 2020 season against the [[Houston Texans]]. He had six carries for 42 rushing yards in the 28–21 victory.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Houston Texans at Pittsburgh Steelers - September 27th, 2020 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202009270pit.htm |access-date=September 28, 2020 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

On September 1, 2021, McFarland was placed on [[injured reserve]] to start the season.<ref>{{cite web|title=Roster moves continue for Steelers|url=https://www.steelers.com/news/roster-moves-continue-for-steelers-x7442|author=Varley, Teresa|website=Steelers.com|date=September 1, 2021}}</ref> He was activated on October 27.<ref>{{cite web|title=Steelers make roster moves|url=https://www.steelers.com/news/steelers-make-roster-moves-x3146|author=Varley, Teresa|website=Steelers.com|date=October 27, 2021|access-date=October 28, 2021|archive-date=October 28, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211028032844/https://www.steelers.com/news/steelers-make-roster-moves-x3146|url-status=dead}}</ref>

On August 30, 2022, McFarland was waived by the Steelers and was signed to the [[practice squad]] the next day.<ref>{{cite web|title=Steelers make two trades; release five players|url=https://www.steelers.com/news/steelers-make-moves-to-get-to-53-man-roster-x8249|author=Varley, Teresa|website=Steelers.com|date=August 30, 2022}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Steelers add eight to practice squad|url=https://www.steelers.com/news/steelers-add-eight-to-practice-squad|author=Varley, Teresa|website=Steelers.com|date=August 31, 2022}}</ref> He signed a reserve/future contract on January 12, 2023.<ref>{{cite web|title=Steelers sign three to Reserve/Future Contracts|url=https://www.steelers.com/news/steelers-sign-three-to-reserve-future-contracts|website=Steelers.com|date=January 12, 2023}}</ref>

On September 18, 2023, McFarland was placed on injured reserve with a knee injury.<ref>{{cite web|title=Steelers make roster moves ahead of MNF|url=https://www.steelers.com/news/steelers-make-roster-moves-ahead-of-mnf|website=Steelers.com|date=September 18, 2023}}</ref> He was activated on November 6.<ref>{{cite web|title=Holcomb placed on IR; McFarland activated|url=https://www.steelers.com/news/holcomb-placed-on-ir-mcfarland-activated|website=Steelers.com|date=November 6, 2023}}</ref> He was released on December 21 and re-signed to the practice squad.<ref name="h412">{{cite web | last=Varley | first=Teresa | title=Steelers release McFarland | website=Steelers.com | date=2023-12-21 | url=https://www.steelers.com/news/steelers-release-mcfarland | access-date=2024-12-27}}</ref> He was not signed to a reserve/future contract after the season and thus became a free agent when his practice squad contract expired.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.steelers.com/news/steelers-sign-17-to-reserve-future-contracts|publisher=[[Pittsburgh Steelers]]|title=Steelers sign 17 to Reserve/Future contracts |author=Varley, Teresa|date=January 17, 2024}}</ref>

=== San Antonio Brahmas (first stint) ===
On February 6, 2024, McFarland signed with the [[San Antonio Brahmas]] of the [[United Football League (2024)|United Football League]] (UFL).<ref>{{Cite web |last=Larsen |first=James |date=2024-02-07 |title=San Antonio Brahmas Add Three Players In UFL Free Agency |url=https://pfnewsroom.com/news/san-antonio-brahmas-add-three-players-in-ufl-free-agency/ |access-date=2024-02-07 |website=Pro Football Newsroom |language=en-US}}</ref> He finished the 2024 season with 337 rushing yards, 249 receiving yards, and 5 total TD's in 7 games. <ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.footballdb.com/players/anthony-mcfarland-mcfaran02 |website=The Football Database |access-date=4 February 2025 |title=Anthony McFarland Football Statistics | the Football Database }}</ref> His contract was terminated on August 19, 2024, to sign with an NFL team.<ref>{{cite tweet |user=UFL_PR |title=The #UFL has announced the following transactions |number=1825644629485650394 |date=August 19, 2024 |access-date=August 20, 2024}}</ref>

===Miami Dolphins===
McFarland signed with the [[Miami Dolphins]] on August 19, 2024.<ref>{{cite news |title=Miami Dolphins Make Roster Moves |url=https://www.miamidolphins.com/news/miami-dolphins-make-roster-moves-8-19-24 |website=MiamiDolphins.com |date=August 19, 2024 |access-date=August 20, 2024}}</ref> He was waived on August 27, and re-signed to the practice squad, but released a day later.<ref>{{Cite web |date=August 27, 2024 |title=Miami Dolphins Make Roster Moves |url=https://www.miamidolphins.com/news/miami-dolphins-make-roster-moves-8-27-24 |access-date=2024-10-30 |website=MiamiDolphins.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=August 28, 2024 |title=Miami Dolphins Make Roster Moves |url=https://www.miamidolphins.com/news/miami-dolphins-make-roster-moves-8-28-24 |access-date=2024-10-30 |website=MiamiDolphins.com}}</ref>

=== San Antonio Brahmas (second stint) ===
On March 6, 2025, McFarland re-signed with the Brahmas.

=== Birmingham Stallions ===
On January 13, 2026, McFarland was selected by the [[Birmingham Stallions (2022)|Birmingham Stallions]] in the 2026 UFL Draft.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Day One of the 2026 UFL Draft Delivers Immediate Impact and Familiar Faces |url=https://www.theufl.com/news/day-one-of-the-2026-ufl-draft-delivers-immediate-impact-and-familiar-faces |access-date=2026-01-14 |website=www.theufl.com |language=en}}</ref>

'''Anthony J. Pittman''' (born November 24, 1996) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[linebacker]]. He played [[college football]] for the [[Wayne State Warriors football|Wayne State Warriors]] and signed with the Lions as an [[undrafted free agent]] in 2019.

== Early life and college ==
Pittman was born on November 24, 1996, and attended [[Birmingham Groves High School]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.nfl.com/players/anthonypittman/profile?id=PIT087988|title=Anthony Pittman|website=NFL.com|language=en|access-date=December 30, 2019}}</ref> Lightly recruited he played [[college football]] at [[Wayne State Warriors football|Wayne State]]. At Wayne State, Pittman was a two-year team captain and two-time first-team all-[[Great Lakes Intercollegiate Athletic Conference]] linebacker.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Schoch |first=Matthew |date=October 18, 2019 |title=Wayne State, Groves LB Anthony Pittman surviving numbers game with Lions |url=https://www.detroitnews.com/story/sports/nfl/lions/2019/10/18/wayne-state-groves-lb-anthony-pittman-surviving-numbers-game-lions/4020872002/ |access-date=December 30, 2019 |website=Detroit News |language=en}}</ref> During his college career, Pittman played in 43 games, recording 181 tackles and 8 sacks.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kirven |first=Jeremiah |date=August 7, 2019 |title=Detroit Lions' Anthony Pittman (Wayne State) eager to do what it takes to make team |url=https://www.freep.com/story/sports/nfl/lions/2019/08/07/detroit-lions-anthony-pittman-wayne-state/1931134001/ |access-date=December 30, 2019 |website=Detroit Free Press |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url=https://wsuathletics.com/sports/football/roster/anthony-pittman/8375 | title=Anthony Pittman - Football }}</ref> Pittman also saw action on special teams for the Warriors.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Schoch |first=Matthew |date=June 5, 2019 |title=Wayne State's Anthony Pittman could carry on Michigan tradition with Lions |url=https://www.detroitnews.com/story/sports/nfl/lions/2019/06/05/anthony-pittman-could-carry-michigan-tradition-detroit-lions/1349647001/ |access-date=December 30, 2019 |website=Detroit News |language=en}}</ref>

===Detroit Lions (first stint)===
Pittman went undrafted in the [[2019 NFL draft]]. He then signed with the [[Detroit Lions]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.theoaklandpress.com/sports/birmingham-s-anthony-pittman-learns-from-best-at-detroit-lions/article_a1a468da-b3d2-11e9-8a55-e7e0b9284fac.html|title=Birmingham's Anthony Pittman learns from best at Detroit Lions training camp|last=Pasche|first=Paula|website=The Oakland Press|language=en|access-date=December 30, 2019|archive-date=December 30, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191230221611/https://www.theoaklandpress.com/sports/birmingham-s-anthony-pittman-learns-from-best-at-detroit-lions/article_a1a468da-b3d2-11e9-8a55-e7e0b9284fac.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> Pittman was waived on August 30, 2019, and signed to the practice squad the next day. He was released from the practice squad on November 5, but re-signed to the practice squad three days later. Pittman was released again from the practice squad on December 3.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://lionswire.usatoday.com/2019/12/04/lions-sign-te-cole-herdman-to-practice-squad-release-lb-anthony-pittman/|title=Lions sign TE Cole Herdman to practice squad, release LB Anthony Pittman|date=December 4, 2019|website=Lions Wire|language=en|access-date=December 30, 2019}}</ref> Pittman was signed again to the practice squad on December 8.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://971theticket.radio.com/articles/press-release/lions-sign-free-agent-lb-anthony-pittman-to-practice-squad|title=Lions Sign Free Agent LB Anthony Pittman To Practice Squad|date=December 9, 2019|website=97.1 The Ticket|language=en|access-date=December 30, 2019}}</ref> Pittman was promoted to the active roster on December 26.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.detroitnews.com/story/sports/nfl/lions/2019/12/27/detroit-lions-promote-wayne-states-anthony-pittman-off-practice-squad/2757008001/|title=Lions promote Wayne State's Anthony Pittman off practice squad|last=Rogers|first=Justin|website=Detroit News|language=en|access-date=December 30, 2019}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.detroitlions.com/news/lions-sign-lb-anthony-pittman-to-active-roster|title=Lions sign LB Anthony Pittman to active roster|website=www.detroitlions.com|language=en-US|access-date=December 30, 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.detroitlions.com/team/transactions/2019 | title=The Official Site of the Detroit Lions }}</ref>

On September 5, 2020, Pittman was waived by the Lions and re-signed to the practice squad the next day.<ref>{{cite web|title=Lions announce roster moves|url=https://www.detroitlions.com/news/lions-announce-roster-moves-x4330|website=DetroitLions.com|date=September 5, 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Lions establish practice squad|url=https://www.detroitlions.com/news/lions-establish-practice-squad|website=DetroitLions.com|date=September 6, 2020}}</ref> He was placed on the practice squad/[[COVID-19]] list by the team on December 22,<ref>{{cite news |title=Anthony Pittman: Placed on COVID-19 list |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/football/news/anthony-pittman-placed-on-covid-19-list/ |website=CBSSports.com |date=December 22, 2020 |access-date=February 5, 2021}}</ref> and restored to the practice squad on January 2, 2021.<ref>{{cite news |title=Anthony Pittman: Restored to practice squad |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/football/news/anthony-pittman-restored-to-practice-squad/ |website=CBSSports.com |date=January 2, 2021 |access-date=February 5, 2021}}</ref> He signed a reserve/future contract with Detroit on January 5.<ref>{{cite web|title=Lions announce Reserve/Future signings|url=https://www.detroitlions.com/news/lions-announce-reserve-future-signings-bolden-kennedy-pittman|website=DetroitLions.com|date=January 5, 2021|access-date=January 12, 2021|archive-date=January 15, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210115134547/https://www.detroitlions.com/news/lions-announce-reserve-future-signings-bolden-kennedy-pittman|url-status=dead}}</ref>

On August 30, 2022, Pittman was waived by the Lions and re-signed to the practice squad the next day.<ref>{{cite web|title=Lions announce roster moves|url=https://www.detroitlions.com/news/lions-announce-roster-moves-x0035|website=DetroitLions.com|date=August 30, 2022|access-date=September 3, 2022|archive-date=January 2, 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230102104838/https://www.detroitlions.com/news/lions-announce-roster-moves-x0035|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Lions announce roster moves|url=https://www.detroitlions.com/news/lions-announce-roster-moves-x6174|website=DetroitLions.com|date=August 31, 2022}}</ref> He was promoted to the active roster on September 27.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.detroitlions.com/team/transactions/2022 | title=The Official Site of the Detroit Lions }}</ref> Pittman played in all 17 regular season games in the 2022 and 2023 seasons for the Lions, as well as all three playoff games in the 2023 season, primarily on special teams.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.commanders.com/news/commanders-sign-lb-anthony-pittman | title=Commanders sign LB Anthony Pittman }}</ref>

===Washington Commanders===
On March 14, 2024, Pittman signed with the [[Washington Commanders]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.commanders.com/news/commanders-sign-lb-anthony-pittman|work=Commanders.com|title=Commanders sign LB Anthony Pittman|date=March 14, 2024|accessdate=March 15, 2024}}</ref> He was released by the Commanders on August 27.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Selby |first1=Zach |title=Commanders release 34 players; place 3 on IR, 1 on PUP list |url=https://www.commanders.com/news/commanders-release-34-players-place-3-on-ir-1-on-pup-list |website=Commanders.com |access-date=August 28, 2024}}</ref>

===Jacksonville Jaguars===
On October 7, 2024, Pittman was signed to the [[Jacksonville Jaguars]] practice squad.<ref>{{cite web|title=Roster Moves: Jaguars Sign LB Anthony Pittman to Practice Squad|url=https://www.jaguars.com/news/k000030-roster-moves-jaguars-sign-lb-anthony-pittman-to-practice-squad|website=Jaguars.com|date=October 7, 2024}}</ref> He played in one game for Jacksonville, and recorded one tackle.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Anthony Pittman Career Stats - NFL |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/player/stats/_/id/4423367/anthony-pittman |access-date=2025-03-16 |website=ESPN |language=en}}</ref>

===Detroit Lions (second stint)===
On December 17, 2024, Pittman was signed by the Detroit Lions off of the Jaguars' practice squad.<ref>{{cite web|title=Detroit Lions place 3 players on IR, add new cornerback to practice squad|url=https://www.prideofdetroit.com/2024/12/17/24323728/detroit-lions-alim-mcneill-carlton-davis-khalil-dorsey-ir-sign-cb-stantley-thomas-oliver|work=Pride of Detroit|date=December 17, 2024}}</ref>

On March 14, 2025, Pittman re-signed with the Lions on a one-year contract.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Reisman |first=Jeremy |date=2025-03-07 |title=Detroit Lions reportedly re-signing LB Anthony Pittman |url=https://www.prideofdetroit.com/2025/3/7/24380220/detroit-lions-reportedly-re-signing-lb-anthony-pittman |access-date=2025-03-16 |website=Pride Of Detroit|publisher=SB Nation |language=en}}</ref> He was released on August 26 as part of final roster cuts, and re-signed to the practice squad.<ref>{{cite web|title=Lions announce roster moves|url=https://www.detroitlions.com/news/detroit-lions-announce-roster-moves-nfl-53-man-2025|website=DetroitLions.com|date=August 26, 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Lions announce roster moves|url=https://www.detroitlions.com/news/lions-announce-roster-moves-x5093|website=DetroitLions.com|date=August 27, 2025}}</ref> Pittman was released on September 9.<ref>{{cite web|title=Detroit Lions add 2 new practice squad players|url=https://www.prideofdetroit.com/detroit-lions-transactions/141425/detroit-lions-add-2-new-practice-squad-players|work=Pride of Detroit|date=September 9, 2025}}</ref>

'''Anthony Ladd''' (born December 23, 1973) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[wide receiver]] for one season with the [[New England Patriots]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He also played in NFL Europe and in the [[Arena Football League]] (AFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Cincinnati Bearcats football|Cincinnati Bearcats]].

==Early life==
Anthony Ladd was born on December 23, 1973, in [[Homestead, Florida]]. He went to high school at Homestead (FL).

==College career==
He went to college at [[Cincinnati Bearcats football|Cincinnati]]. In 1993 he had 10 catches for 170 yards.<ref name="auto4">{{Cite web|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/anthony-ladd-1.html|title=Anthony Ladd College Stats|website=College Football at Sports-Reference.com}}</ref> In 1994 he had 35 catches for 446 yards and 3 touchdowns.<ref name="auto4"/> The next year he had 34 catches for 433 yards and three touchdowns. He also had one rush for 5 yards.<ref name="auto4"/> His final year of college he had 21 catches for 409 yards and three touchdowns.<ref name="auto4"/>

===Berlin Thunder===
In 2000, he played for the [[Berlin Thunder]]. He played in 10 games and had 19 catches for 238 yards and three touchdowns.<ref name="auto2"/><ref name="auto1"/>

===Chicago Rush===
In 2001, he played for the [[Chicago Rush]] of the [[Arena Football League]]. He played in 3 games and had 8 catches for 87 yards. He also had three touchdowns.<ref name="auto1"/> In 2002 he played for them and had 41 catches for 449 yards and 13 touchdowns.<ref name="auto1"/><ref name="auto3">{{Cite web|url=http://www.arenafan.com/players/Anthony_Ladd-2330/|title=Anthony Ladd | ArenaFan.com|website=www.arenafan.com}}</ref> He also had 4 rushes for 2 yards and a touchdown.<ref name="auto3"/> The next year he had 33 catches for 402 yards and 11 touchdowns. He also had 2 rushing touchdowns.<ref name="auto3"/> He even had 2 interceptions on defense.<ref name="auto1"/> His final season was 2004, where he played for 3 teams. With the Rush, he had 8 catches for 65 yards and 2 touchdowns.<ref name="auto1"/>

===Dallas Desperado===
His second team of 2004 was the [[Dallas Desperados]].<ref name="auto1"/> With them he had 4 catches for 31 yards.<ref name="auto1"/>

===Las Vegas Gladiators===
His final team was the [[Las Vegas Gladiators]]. He had 3 catches for 36 yards with them.<ref name="auto1"/>

'''Anthony Dashawn Richardson Sr.''' (born May 22, 2002) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[quarterback]] for the [[Indianapolis Colts]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Florida Gators football|Florida Gators]] and was selected by the Colts fourth overall in the [[2023 NFL draft]].

==Early life==
Richardson was born on May 22, 2002, in [[Miami|Miami, Florida]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Brugler |first=Dane |title=The Beast: 2023 NFL Draft Guide |url=https://cdn.theathletic.com/app/uploads/2023/04/10111751/TheBeast_NFL_Draft_Guide-1.pdf |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230410190932/https://cdn.theathletic.com/app/uploads/2023/04/10111751/TheBeast_NFL_Draft_Guide-1.pdf |url-status=dead |archive-date=April 10, 2023 |url-access=subscription |access-date=April 10, 2022 |website=[[The Athletic]] |pages=6}}</ref> He later attended [[Loften High School]] in [[Gainesville, Florida]]. However, Richardson played [[quarterback]] for [[Eastside High School (Gainesville, Florida)|Eastside High School's]] football team.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Carter |first=Scott |date=December 21, 2019 |title=Hometown QB Richardson a Future Netflix Star with Shot to Star Someday for Gators |url=https://floridagators.com/news/2019/12/21/football-anthony-richardson-feature.aspx |access-date=2024-06-03 |website=Florida Gators |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Atkins |first=Nate |date=September 6, 2023 |title=Chasing Tim Tebow, idolizing Tom Brady, fighting fires: Making of Colts QB Anthony Richardson |url=https://www.indystar.com/story/sports/nfl/colts/2023/09/06/nfl-indianapolis-colts-anthony-richardson-high-school-florida-gators-history/70758683007/ |access-date=2024-06-03 |website=The Indianapolis Star |language=en-US}}</ref> During his high school career, Richardson had 4,633 passing yards with 37 passing touchdowns to go along with 1,633 rushing yards and 41 touchdowns.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Anthony Richardson - Football |url=https://floridagators.com/sports/football/roster/anthony--richardson/15233 |access-date=2024-06-03 |website=Florida Gators |language=en}}</ref> He committed to play [[college football]] at the [[University of Florida]].<ref>{{Cite magazine |last=Goodall |first=Zach |date=December 18, 2019 |title=QB Anthony Richardson Signs With Florida |url=https://www.si.com/college/florida/recruiting/breaking-qb-anthony-richardson-signs-with-florida |magazine=Sports Illustrated |language=en |access-date=June 1, 2023}}</ref>

==College career==
Richardson appeared in just four games during his first year at [[Florida Gators football|Florida]] in 2020, completing one of two passes for 27 yards with a touchdown and interception.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Thompson |first=Edgar |date=August 26, 2021 |title=UF QB, Gainesville native Anthony Richardson aims to elevate Gators from backup role |url=https://www.orlandosentinel.com/sports/florida-gators/os-sp-gators-football-0827-20210826-hqfm6kgnuzggregbbmmblxk4mm-story.html |access-date=June 1, 2023 |website=Orlando Sentinel}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Hall |first=Graham |date=August 25, 2021 |title=Anthony Richardson 'blessed' with opportunity to improve and inspire with Gators |url=https://www.gatorsports.com/story/football/2021/08/25/florida-gators-quarterback-anthony-richardson-has-prepared-if-he-starter/5596982001/ |access-date=June 1, 2023 |website=Gator Sports}}</ref> He was able to [[Redshirt (college sports)|redshirt]] his first year of collegiate eligibility.<ref>{{Cite web |last=de la Torre |first=Nick |date=June 22, 2021 |title=Redshirt Freshman Report: Anthony Richardson |url=https://florida.rivals.com/news/redshirt-freshman-report-anthony-richardson |access-date=June 17, 2023 |website=1standTenFlorida}}</ref> Richardson entered 2021 as the backup to [[Emory Jones]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bender |first=Bill |date=September 18, 2021 |title=Who is Anthony Richardson? Meet Florida Gators' redshirt freshman QB sensation |url=https://www.sportingnews.com/us/ncaa-football/news/anthony-richardson-florida-gators/1611le6ug8kpw1nw1t5m1auwot |access-date=June 1, 2023 |website=Sporting News}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Taylor |first=G. Allan |date=August 27, 2021 |title='Dynamic' Emory Jones, talented Anthony Richardson form 1–2 punch: Rating the Gators' QB combination |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/2791111/2021/08/27/dynamic-jones-talented-richardson-form-1-2-punch-inside-the-gators-qb-battle/ |access-date=June 1, 2023 |website=The Athletic}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Heim |first=Mark |date=September 11, 2021 |title=A Florida QB controversy after Anthony Richardson replaces Emory Jones ahead of Alabama game? |url=https://www.al.com/sec/2021/09/a-florida-qb-controversy-after-anthony-richardson-replaces-emory-jones-ahead-of-alabama-game.html |access-date=June 1, 2023 |website=AL.com}}</ref> Against the [[2021 LSU Tigers football team|LSU Tigers]], he replaced Jones and completed 10 of 19 passes for 167 yards, three touchdowns, and two interceptions to go along with a rushing touchdown.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Thompson |first=Edgar |date=October 17, 2021 |title=In loss to LSU, Gators find hope and possibly a new starting QB in Anthony Richardson |url=https://www.orlandosentinel.com/sports/florida-gators/os-sp-gators-football-lsu-1017-20211016-fzgohwwxrvffrkhihgksmjcdm4-story.html |access-date=June 1, 2023 |website=Orlando Sentinel}}</ref>[[File:Anthony_Richardson_2022.jpg|thumb|left|Richardson in 2022]]Richardson officially became the starting quarterback for the Gators in 2022. In the first game of the season, he helped lead a 29–26 upset over the seventh-ranked [[Utah Utes football|Utah Utes]] on September 3, 2022.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Long |first=Mark |date=September 4, 2022 |title=Richardson, Burney help Florida upset No. 7 Utah in Swamp |url=https://www.sandiegouniontribune.com/sports/national/story/2022-09-03/richardson-burney-help-florida-upset-no-7-utah-in-swamp |access-date=June 1, 2023 |website=San Diego Union-Tribune |language=en |agency=Associated Press}}</ref> On September 24, in a 38–33 loss to the [[2022 Tennessee Volunteers football team|Tennessee Volunteers]], Richardson had 453 passing yards, two touchdowns, and an interception to go along with 17 carries for 62 yards and two touchdowns.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Florida at Tennessee Box Score, September 24, 2022 |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/boxscores/2022-09-24-tennessee.html |access-date=June 17, 2023 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

Overall, in 2022, Richardson played in 12 games and passed for 2,549 yards, 17 touchdowns and nine interceptions, as well as rushing for 654 yards and 9 touchdowns in his first full season as a starting quarterback for a college team.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Anthony Richardson 2022 Game Log |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/anthony-richardson-2/gamelog/2022 |access-date=2024-06-03 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> During his time at Florida, Richardson amassed a 6–6 record as the starting quarterback for the Gators.<ref>{{Cite web |date=March 4, 2023 |title=Anthony Richardson breaks multiple QB records at NFL combine |url=https://www.foxsports.com/stories/nfl/anthony-richardson-breaks-multiple-qb-records-at-nfl-combine |access-date=2024-06-03 |website=FOX Sports |language=en-US}}</ref>

As a collegiate player, Richardson was stated to have displayed "dynamic talent" as a passer and runner during his college years but lacked accuracy and consistency.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Adelson |first=Andrea |date=2023-04-21 |title=The Anthony Richardson quandary: 'Superhuman' talent, underwhelming accuracy |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/36235928/why-nfl-draft-prospect-anthony-richardson-says-not-earth |access-date=2024-10-29 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}}</ref> Richardson's physical gifts also helped propel him as a possible first-round NFL draft selection.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Jeyarajah |first=Shehan|date=December 5, 2022 |title=2023 NFL Draft: Florida QB Anthony Richardson declares after flashing dynamic talent in inconsistent season |url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-football/news/2023-nfl-draft-florida-qb-anthony-richardson-declares-after-flashing-dynamic-talent-in-inconsistent-season/|access-date=December 5, 2022 |website=CBS Sports}}</ref> Following the end of the 2022 season, Richardson announced that he would enter the [[2023 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bromberg |first=Nick |date=December 5, 2022 |title=Florida QB Anthony Richardson declares for 2023 NFL draft |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/florida-qb-anthony-richardson-declares-for-2023-nfl-draft-182319978.html |access-date=January 9, 2023 |website=Yahoo! Sports}}</ref>

===2023===
{{See also|2023 Indianapolis Colts season}}
Richardson was drafted in the first round by the [[Indianapolis Colts]] with the fourth overall pick in the [[2023 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Simmons |first=Myles |date=2023-04-27 |title=Colts select Anthony Richardson with No. 4 overall pick |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/profootballtalk/rumor-mill/news/colts-select-anthony-richardson-with-no-4-overall-pick |access-date=2024-06-03 |website=NBC Sports |language=en-US}}</ref> 

[[File:Anthony Richardson Colts 2023 season (cropped).png|thumb|Richardson in 2023]]
During his first training camp with the Colts, Richardson underwent nasal septum surgery to improve his breathing.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Simmons |first=Myles  |date=July 31, 2023 |title=Shane Steichen: Anthony Richardson nasal procedure is "nothing serious" |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/profootballtalk/rumor-mill/news/shane-steichen-anthony-richardson-nasal-procedure-is-nothing-serious |access-date=July 31, 2023 |website=NBC Sports |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Bowen |first=Kevin |date=July 31, 2023 |title=Colts Training Camp Notebook Day 4: Anthony Richardson Has Nose Surgery |url=https://1075thefan.com/95927/colts-training-camp-notebook-day-4-anthony-richardson-has-nose-surgery/ |access-date=July 31, 2023 |website=93.5 / 107.5 The Fan |language=en-US}}</ref> On August 15, 2023, Richardson was named by head coach [[Shane Steichen]] as the Colts' starting quarterback over [[Gardner Minshew]] and [[Sam Ehlinger]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.colts.com/news/anthony-richardson-starting-quarterback-2023-regular-season-gardner-minshew |title=Colts name Anthony Richardson starting quarterback for 2023 regular season |last=Stankevitz |first=JJ |website=Colts.com |date=August 15, 2023 |access-date=August 15, 2023}}</ref>

Richardson made his NFL debut in the season-opener against the [[Jacksonville Jaguars]]. He threw his first touchdown pass to [[Michael Pittman Jr.]], ran for a touchdown, and threw his first career interception to [[Tyson Campbell]] in the 31–21 loss.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Jaguars 31–21 Colts (Sep 10, 2023) Box Score |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/boxscore/_/gameId/401547404 |access-date=September 11, 2023 |website=ESPN |language=en}}</ref> During Week 2 against the [[Houston Texans]], Richardson ran for two touchdowns before leaving the eventual 31–20 road victory with a concussion in the second quarter as a result of a hit taken as he scored his second touchdown.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Colts 31–20 Texans (Sep 17, 2023) Final Score |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/game/_/gameId/401547419 |access-date=September 19, 2023 |website=ESPN |language=en}}</ref> On September 22, Richardson was declared out in Week 3 due to a concussion he suffered against the Texans.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Holder |first=Stephen |date=September 22, 2023 |title=Colts rule out QB Richardson against Ravens |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/38462419/colts-qb-anthony-richardson-protocol-vs-ravens |access-date=September 22, 2023 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}}</ref> He returned the following week against the [[Los Angeles Rams]] and recorded two passing touchdowns and a rushing touchdown, erasing a 23-point deficit in a 29–23 overtime loss.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Rams 29–23 Colts (Oct 1, 2023) Final Score |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/game/_/gameId/401547449 |access-date=October 3, 2023 |website=ESPN |language=en}}</ref> His rushing touchdown in this game marked the first time in NFL history that a rookie quarterback had scored a rushing touchdown in each of his first three starts.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Miller |first=Natalie |date=October 2, 2023 |title=Colts QB Anthony Richardson sets rookie rushing record |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/colts-qb-anthony-richardson-sets-123330929.html |access-date=October 3, 2023 |website=Yahoo! Sports |language=en}}</ref> On October 9, Richardson was placed on injured reserve due to a grade three [[AC joint]] sprain he suffered in Week 5 against the [[Tennessee Titans]], which was initially announced for him to miss one-to-two months.<ref>{{Cite web |last=White |first=Brenna |date=October 9, 2023 |title=Colts QB Anthony Richardson suffers Grade 3 AC joint sprain, to miss one month or more |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/colts-qb-anthony-richardson-suffers-ac-joint-sprain-to-miss-one-month-or-more |access-date=October 11, 2023 |website=NFL.com}}</ref> On October 18, the Colts announced that Richardson would miss the rest of the season, and he successfully underwent shoulder surgery to repair the sprain six days later.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Holder |first=Stephen |date=October 18, 2023 |title=Colts' Anthony Richardson to have season-ending shoulder surgery |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/38687404/colts-anthony-richardson-season-ending-shoulder-surgery |access-date=October 18, 2023 |publisher=ESPN}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Stankevitz |first=JJ |date=October 25, 2023 |title=Colts QB Anthony Richardson undergoes successful shoulder surgery |url=https://www.colts.com/news/anthony-richardson-successful-shoulder-surgery-update-shane-steichen |access-date=October 28, 2023 |website=Indianapolis Colts}}</ref>

===2024===
{{See also|2024 Indianapolis Colts season}}
Richardson opened the season as the Colts' starter after recovering from shoulder surgery the previous year. He missed Weeks 5 and 6 with an oblique injury.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Holder |first1=Stephen |title=Despite injuries, Colts letting QB Anthony Richardson run |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/41929855/indianapolis-colts-running-quarterback-anthony-richardson |access-date=October 29, 2024 |work=ESPN |date=October 22, 2024}}</ref> In Week 8 against the Texans, Richardson completed 10 of 32 passes for 175 yards, a touchdown, and an interception. He also voluntarily took himself out for one play in the third quarter, stating that he "needed a breather" as the Colts lost 23–20.<ref>{{cite news |last=Holder |first=Stephen |title=Richardson 'needed a breather' in second half of Colts' loss |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/42040546/richardson-needed-breather-second-half-colts-loss |access-date=October 29, 2024 |work=ESPN |date=October 27, 2024}}</ref> Richardson was benched the following week in favor of backup quarterback [[Joe Flacco]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Myles |first1=Simmons |title=Colts bench Anthony Richardson for Joe Flacco |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/profootballtalk/rumor-mill/news/colts-bench-anthony-richardson-for-joe-flacco |access-date=29 October 2024 |work=NBC Sports |publisher=NBCUniversal |date=29 October 2024}}</ref> Prior to the benching, Richardson had generated an NFL-worst 44.4% completion percentage in six games.<ref>{{cite news |last=Patra |first=Kevin |title=Colts to bench Anthony Richardson, plan to start Joe Flacco vs. Vikings on Sunday |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/colts-to-start-qb-joe-flacco-over-anthony-richardson-vs-vikings |access-date=October 29, 2024 |work=NFL.com |date=October 29, 2024}}</ref>

After two losses with Flacco, the Colts announced that Richardson would be the starter for the remainder of the season, beginning in their Week 11 matchup against the [[New York Jets]].<ref>{{cite news |last=Shook |first=Nick |title=Colts name QB Anthony Richardson starter for rest of season; Joe Flacco benched after two games |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/colts-name-qb-anthony-richardson-starter-2024-season-joe-flacco-benched |access-date=November 14, 2024 |date=November 13, 2024}}</ref> In his return as starter, Richardson completed 67% of his passes for a career-high 272 yards, a touchdown, and added two rushing scores, including the game-winner in the final minute as the Colts won 28–27.<ref>{{cite news |last=Stankevitz |first=JJ |title=Anthony Richardson returns from benching relaxed, confident and in control to push Colts past Jets in Week 11 |url=https://www.colts.com/news/anthony-richardson-benching-return-new-york-jets-win-week-11-shane-steichen |access-date=November 18, 2024 |work=Colts.com |date=November 17, 2024}}</ref> In Week 13, Richardson orchestrated a 19-play, 80-yard touchdown drive, capped off with a go-ahead two-point conversion with under 15 seconds left as the Colts came back to win 25–24 over the [[New England Patriots]].<ref>{{cite news |last=Stankevitz |first=JJ |title=Colts bypass tie, Anthony Richardson powers in game-winning two-point conversion to beat Patriots in Week 13 |url=https://www.colts.com/news/colts-bypass-tie-anthony-richardson-powers-in-game-winning-two-point-conversion-to-beat-patriots-in-week-13 |access-date=December 1, 2024 |work=Colts.com |date=December 1, 2024}}</ref> Richardson missed the final two games of the season with a back injury as the Colts missed the playoffs with a loss in Week 17 to the [[New York Giants]]. He finished the season completing 47.7 percent of his 264 passing attempts for 1,814 yards, eight touchdowns, and 12 interceptions. He also rushed 86 times for 499 yards with six touchdowns.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Stankevitz |first1=JJ |title=Colts QB Anthony Richardson: 'I expect more out of myself' as critical offseason begins |url=https://www.colts.com/news/anthony-richardson-2025-offseason-expectations-competition-free-agent-quarterback-nfl-draft |access-date=August 19, 2025 |work=Colts.com |date=January 6, 2025}}</ref>

=== 2025 ===
{{See also|2025 Indianapolis Colts season}}
With the signing of quarterback [[Daniel Jones (American football)|Daniel Jones]] in March 2025, Richardson opened the offseason in a competition with Jones for the starting quarterback job.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Holder |first1=Stephen |title=Colts' Steichen nears decision in Jones - Richardson QB race |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/45996656/colts-steichen-nears-decision-jones-richardson-qb-race |access-date=August 19, 2025 |work=ESPN |date=August 16, 2025}}</ref> On August 19, Jones was named the starter, with Richardson named a backup to begin his third NFL season.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Stankevitz |first1=JJ |title=Shane Steichen names Daniel Jones Colts' starting quarterback |url=https://www.colts.com/news/daniel-jones-starting-quarterback-qb1-shane-steichen-anthony-richardson |access-date=August 19, 2025 |work=Colts.com |date=August 19, 2025}}</ref> On October 13, Richardson was placed on [[Injured reserve list#NFL rules|injured reserve]] after he fractured the [[orbital bone]] in his eye during pregame warmups the previous day.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/nfl/breaking-news/article/colts-qb-anthony-richardson-placed-on-injured-reserve-after-fluke-accident-with-workout-band-that-resulted-in-orbital-fracture-203643583.html|title=Colts QB Anthony Richardson placed on injured reserve after 'fluke accident' with workout band that resulted in orbital fracture|work=Yahoo! Sports|date=October 13, 2025|accessdate=December 4, 2025|first=Ryan|last=Young}}</ref>

===2026===
{{See also|2026 Indianapolis Colts season}}
On April 30, 2026, the Colts declined the fifth-year option on Richardson's contract, making him a free agent after the 2026 season.<ref>{{cite web|title=Colts decline fifth-year option for Anthony Richardson|url=https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/profootballtalk/rumor-mill/news/colts-decline-fifth-year-option-for-anthony-richardson|author=Williams, Charean|work=Pro Football Talk|publisher=NBC Sports|date=April 30, 2026}}</ref>

He played [[college football]] for the [[Baldwin Wallace Yellow Jackets football|Baldwin Wallace Yellow Jackets]] and was signed by the [[Tennessee Titans]] as an [[Free agent#Undrafted free agent|undrafted free agent]] after the [[2023 NFL draft]]. ==Early life and college== Kendall was born on December 17, 1999, in [[El Paso, Texas]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/player/_/id/5143279/anthony-kendall|publisher=[[ESPN]]|title=Anthony Kendall}}{{Cite web|url=https://www.tennesseetitans.com/team/players-roster/anthony-kendall/|publisher=[[Tennessee Titans]]|title=Anthony Kendall}} He attended [[Anclote High School]] before transferring to [[River Ridge High School (Florida)|River Ridge High School]], playing football in all four years while also being a member of the track, basketball and weightlifting teams. In the [[COVID-19]]-shortened spring 2021 season, he played two games and was named honorable mention all-conference with 13 tackles. In the fall 2021 season, Kendall played seven games and had 11 tackles. He had his best season as a [[Senior (education)|senior]] in 2022, having 56 tackles and three [[interception]]s while being named [[College Football All-America Team|All-American]] and the
